definition_en: to succeed in reaching a goal or producing a result through effort
core_image: 终点线在最后一步被跨过
scene: 长跑最后一段，他咬紧牙关，把训练了几个月的目标一步步追近。She achieved her goal after two years of steady practice.
sceneCN: 这里 achieve 是「实现、达到」（第 1 个义项：经过努力达成目标）；句意为经过两年稳定练习，她实现了目标。

senses.title: Reach a goal
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力成功抵达目标
senses.example: She achieved her goal after two years of steady practice.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两年稳定练习，她实现了目标。
senses.why: French achever meant 'to bring to a head, to finish', so the verb pictures a task carried through to its end.
senses.whyCN: 法语 achever 意为「做到头、完成」，因此这个动词描绘把任务做到终点。

senses.title: Produce a result
senses.definition: to bring about a result, especially a good one
senses.definitionCN: 产生某种结果，尤指好结果
senses.example: The new method achieved a sharp drop in waste.
senses.exampleCN: 新方法使浪费大幅下降。
senses.why: The same effort that finishes a task also produces a measurable result, so achieve names both the reaching and the yielding.
senses.whyCN: 完成任务的同一份努力也产出可衡量的结果，因此 achieve 兼指「达到」与「取得」。

intro.en: Achieve comes from Old French achever, 'to finish', from the phrase a chief, 'to a head', built on Latin caput, 'head'.
intro.cn: achieve 来自古法语 achever（完成），源自短语 a chief（到头），由拉丁语 caput（头）构成。

items.cn: caput 意为「头」，是 capital 与 chef 的来源。

items.cn: ad caput 意为「到头、到终点」。

items.en: achever meant 'to finish, bring to a head'.
items.cn: achever 意为「完成、做到头」。

items.en: English achieve first meant 'to finish a task'.
items.cn: 英语 achieve 最初意为「完成一项任务」。

items.en: modern usage adds achieve a goal, success, and recognition.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了 achieve a goal、achieve success 与 achieve recognition。

scene: 毕业典礼上，校长念出一串名字，每个名字后面都跟着一项多年的成果。Winning the scholarship was her greatest achievement.

senses.title: Something successfully done
senses.definition: a thing done successfully with effort and skill
senses.definitionCN: 经努力与技巧成功做成之事
senses.example: Winning the scholarship was her greatest achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 获得奖学金是她最大的成就。

senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀把动词变成结果，因此 achievement 指做成之事，而非努力本身。

senses.example: The achievement of clean water for the village took years.

definition_en: to admit that something is true, to confirm that something has arrived, or to show thanks for help
core_image: 收到信后抬手回一句「我知道了」
scene: 会议上有人指出报告里的漏洞，负责人沉默片刻，点头认下。He acknowledged the mistake without making excuses.

senses.title: Admit the truth
senses.definition: to accept that something is true or exists
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真或确实存在
senses.example: He acknowledged the mistake without making excuses.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认了错误，没有找借口。
senses.why: The word grew from 'to know': to acknowledge is to let knowledge of a fact stand openly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「知道」生长而来：acknowledge 就是公开承认自己知道某个事实。

senses.title: Confirm receipt
senses.definition: to tell someone that a message or item has arrived
senses.definitionCN: 告知对方信息或物品已经收到
senses.example: Please acknowledge receipt of this letter.
senses.exampleCN: 请确认收到此信。
senses.why: In offices the verb became a formal signal: a reply proves the message landed.
senses.whyCN: 在办公场合这个动词成了正式信号：一封回执证明信息已送达。

senses.title: Show thanks
senses.definition: to express thanks or credit for help
senses.definitionCN: 对帮助表示感谢或注明出处
senses.example: The author acknowledged her research team in the preface.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在序言中感谢了她的研究团队。
senses.why: To know a debt of help is also to admit it, so the same verb covers thanks.
senses.whyCN: 知道受了帮助也是一种承认，因此同一个动词也涵盖致谢。

过去分词作形容词，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: Obtain something
senses.definition: to come to own or possess something
senses.definitionCN: 开始拥有或占有某物
senses.example: He acquired a rare map at the auction.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍卖会上得到一幅稀有的地图。
senses.why: Latin acquirere meant 'to get in addition', built on quaerere, 'to seek', so the word pictures a successful search.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acquirere 意为「额外取得」，由 quaerere（寻求）构成，因此这个词描绘一次成功的寻找。

senses.title: Gain a skill or habit
senses.definition: to develop a skill, habit, or quality through time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间发展出技能、习惯或品质
senses.example: She acquired a good command of French during two years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她旅居两年，掌握了不错的法语。
senses.why: Skills are also 'got', but slowly; the same verb covers knowledge that grows rather than objects bought.
senses.whyCN: 技能也是「得到」，只是更慢；同一个动词也涵盖逐渐生长的知识，而不只是买来的物品。

intro.en: Acquire comes from Latin acquirere, 'to get in addition', from ad- 'to' and quaerere, 'to seek'.
intro.cn: acquire 来自拉丁语 acquirere（额外取得），由 ad-（向）与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: quaerere meant 'to seek, to ask', the root of query and question.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、询问」，是 query 与 question 的词根。

items.en: acquirere meant 'to get in addition, to gain'.
items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外取得、获得」。

items.en: Old French passed the verb toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词传向英语。

items.en: English acquire first meant 'to gain possession'.
items.cn: 英语 acquire 最初意为「取得占有」。

items.en: modern usage adds acquire a skill and acquire a company.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了掌握技能与收购公司。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and adjective family; the second gathers verbs of getting something.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与形容词词族；第二组收表示获得的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or thing obtained.
The adjective meaning 'eager to get things'.
The adjective for something gained later, not innate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「后天获得的」

entries.definition: To get something, often by effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，常指经努力。

entries.definition: To get something useful or valuable.
To obtain something with care or difficulty.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the seeking root and the bookshop scene; the abstract hooks picture a hand reaching for a shelf.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「寻求」词根与书店场景；抽象记忆点想象伸手去拿货架上的东西。

normal.en: Acquire is 'seek and get': quaerere means seek.
normal.cn: acquire 是「寻求并得到」：quaerere 意为寻求。

normal.en: Acquire knowledge is slower than acquire a car.
normal.cn: acquire knowledge 比 acquire a car 慢得多。

normal.en: The noun is acquisition, common in business.
normal.cn: 名词是 acquisition，商业中常用。

normal.en: Acquired means gained later, not born with.
normal.cn: acquired 指后天获得，而非天生。

normal.en: Obtain is formal; get is neutral; acquire is formal and slightly technical.
normal.cn: obtain 正式，get 中性，acquire 正式且略专业。

abstract.en: Picture a hand taking a book from a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从架上取下一本书。

abstract.en: Picture a skill growing through daily practice.
abstract.cn: 想象技能在日常练习中生长。

abstract.en: Picture a company signing a purchase deal.
abstract.cn: 想象公司签下收购协议。

examples.en: He acquired a rare map at the auction.
examples.cn: 他在拍卖会上得到一幅稀有的地图。

examples.en: She acquired a good command of French during two years abroad.
examples.cn: 她旅居两年，掌握了不错的法语。

examples.en: The firm acquired a smaller rival last spring.
examples.cn: 该公司去年春天收购了一家较小的对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夸尔」——一路寻求，最后把东西放进自己的篮子。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ quaerere（寻求）→ acquirere（取得）；核心义是「寻而求得」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from obtaining an object, to gaining a skill or habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从取得物品，走到获得技能或习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a shelf
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去拿货架上的东西

branches.en: To come to own something.
branches.cn: 开始拥有某物。

branches.en: To develop a skill or habit.
branches.cn: 发展出技能或习惯。

branches.en: Objects and skills are both gained over time.
branches.cn: 物品与技能都随时间获得。

branches.en: Acquisition in business is the same verb at company scale.
branches.cn: 商业收购是同一动词在公司尺度上的用法。

branches.en: Acquired taste is the clearest bridge between the senses.
branches.cn: acquired taste 是两个义项之间最清楚的桥梁。

intro.en: The verb joins the prefix ac- (to) with the seeking root quir- and the verb ending -e, and its family adds noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: 这个动词把前缀 ac-（向）与「寻求」词根 quir- 及动词词尾 -e 结合，词族另加名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acquirere is the direct ancestor, recorded here with the verb quaerere that lies behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acquirere 是直接祖先，这里连同其背后的 quaerere 一并记录。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「获得；收购」
形容词，义为「贪得的」

definition_zh: 启动；激活；使活化；使进入现役
definition_en: to make something start working, become active, or become chemically or biologically effective
core_image: 按下开关，沉睡的机器开始转动
scene: 实验室的新设备装好后，技术员按下开关，让整套系统开始运转。The technician pressed the switch to activate the new system.
sceneCN: 这里 activate 是「启动」（第 1 个义项：使设备开始工作）；句意为技术员按下开关，让新系统开始运转。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「激活；启动」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「激活剂；启动器」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「停用；关闭」
由 deactivate 加名词后缀构成，义为「停用；解除激活」

senses.title: To start a device
senses.definition: to make a machine, alarm, or system begin to operate
senses.definitionCN: 使机器、警报或系统开始运行
senses.example: The technician pressed the switch to activate the new system.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员按下开关，让新系统开始运转。
senses.why: The Latin root agere is 'to do', and to activate is to set something into doing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 agere 意为「做」，activate 就是让某物进入「做」的状态。

senses.title: To set a plan in motion
senses.definition: to cause a plan, process, or procedure to begin
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、流程或程序开始
senses.example: The committee activated the emergency plan at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在黎明时启动了应急方案。
senses.why: A plan is dormant until switched on, just as a machine is.
senses.whyCN: 计划在启动之前处于休眠状态，就像机器一样。

senses.title: To make chemically reactive
senses.definition: to treat a substance so that it can react more readily
senses.definitionCN: 处理某物质，使其更容易参与反应
senses.example: Heat activated the catalyst before the gas was introduced.
senses.exampleCN: 在通入气体之前，加热使催化剂活化。
senses.why: Activation lowers the barrier that keeps a reaction asleep.
senses.whyCN: 活化降低了让反应保持沉睡的能垒。

senses.title: To switch on a gene or cell
senses.definition: to cause a gene, enzyme, or cell to begin functioning
senses.definitionCN: 使基因、酶或细胞开始发挥作用
senses.example: The protein activated a gene that controls cell repair.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛋白质激活了一个控制细胞修复的基因。
senses.why: A gene has an on state and an off state, and activation turns the switch to on.
senses.whyCN: 基因有开启与关闭两种状态，激活就是把开关拨到开启。

senses.title: To call a military unit into service
senses.definition: to bring a reserve unit or a piece of equipment into active duty
senses.definitionCN: 使预备役部队或装备转入现役
senses.example: The governor activated the national guard after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，州长调动国民警卫队进入现役。
senses.why: Reserve forces exist but are inactive until a formal order activates them.
senses.whyCN: 预备役力量存在但并不活动，直到正式命令把它们激活。

senses.title: To activate software or a licence
senses.definition: to register or unlock a piece of software or a licence so that it can be used
senses.definitionCN: 对软件或授权进行注册或解锁，使其可以使用
senses.example: You must activate the program before the trial period ends.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在试用期结束前激活这个程序。
senses.why: Digital activation is a modern switch that changes a locked product into a working one.
senses.whyCN: 数字激活是现代版的开关，把锁定的产品变成可用的产品。

senses.title: To open a facility for use
senses.definition: to put a building, service, or public system into operation
senses.definitionCN: 让建筑、服务或公共系统投入运行
senses.example: The city activated the new water treatment plant in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 城市在春天启用了新的水处理厂。
senses.why: A plant is built but idle; activating it is the moment it joins the working network.
senses.whyCN: 工厂建好但闲置；启用就是它接入运转网络的时刻。

senses.title: To stimulate demand or a response
senses.definition: to trigger activity in a market, a system, or a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在市场、系统或人群中触发活动
senses.example: The campaign activated demand for the older product line.
senses.exampleCN: 这场推广激发了对旧产品线的需求。
senses.why: Demand can lie dormant, and the verb pictures a switch that sets it moving.
senses.whyCN: 需求可能处于沉睡状态，这个动词描绘的正是把它启动起来的开关。

intro.en: Activate is a Latin-derived verb built on the adjective for active, which itself comes from the verb 'to do'.
intro.cn: activate 是拉丁语来源的动词，建立在表示「活跃」的形容词上，而那个形容词又来自「做」这个动词。

items.en: *ag- is generally reconstructed as 'to drive, do'. The deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ag- 表示「驱动、做」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: agere meant 'to do, drive, act', the source of actor, agenda and action.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、行动」，是 actor、agenda 与 action 的来源。

items.en: The participle actus and the adjective activus grew from agere, giving the idea of being in action.
items.cn: 分词 actus 与形容词 activus 从 agere 生长出来，形成「处于行动中」的概念。

items.en: activating forms of medieval Latin are recorded with the sense 'to make active'; the exact earliest use is uncertain.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中已见到表示「使活动」的 activare 形式；确切的最早用法不确定。

items.en: English activate appears in scientific and technical writing; its first recorded date is source uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 activate 出现在科学与技术写作中；确切首见年代来源不确定。

items.en: Modern usage covers machines, plans, genes, soldiers, software and markets.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖机器、计划、基因、部队、软件与市场。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agere family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of beginning or energising.
note.cn: 形近组收 agere 词族；近义组收表示开始或供能的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something active or operational.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激活、启动」，指使某物活动或投入运行的行为。

entries.definition: A substance or device that starts a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激活剂、启动器」，指启动某个过程的物质或装置。

entries.definition: To switch something off or make it inactive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停用、关闭」，使某物停止活动。

entries.definition: Ready to respond or react; built on the same act- stem with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反应的、易起反应的」；同一 act- 词干加不同前缀构成。

entries.definition: The state of being busy or the things people do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「活动、忙碌状态」，指人们所做的事或忙碌的状况。

entries.definition: To begin doing something or to make something begin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始」，开始做某事或使某事开始。

entries.definition: To cause an event to happen suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「触发」，使事件突然发生。

entries.definition: To make something possible or give it the power to work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」，使某事成为可能或赋予其运作能力。

entries.definition: To give energy or power to a system or a person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供能、激励」，给系统或人提供能量。

entries.definition: To encourage activity or growth in something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刺激、促进」，鼓励某物产生活动或增长。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the agere root, the on-off image, and the many contexts where activation happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 agere 词根、开与关的意象，以及激活发生的多种场景。

normal.en: agere is 'to do': activating something is making it do again.
normal.cn: agere 是「做」：激活某物就是让它重新开始做。

normal.en: The same root gives action, actor and agenda, all about doing.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 action、actor 与 agenda，都与「做」有关。

normal.en: Activation is the noun, activator the thing that switches it on, and deactivate the reverse.
normal.cn: activation 是名词，activator 是启动它的东西，deactivate 则是反向操作。

normal.en: Activated carbon is charcoal treated so that it can absorb much more.
normal.cn: activated carbon 是经过处理、吸附能力大大增强的炭。

normal.en: In computing, activate unlocks a product; in the military, it brings a reserve unit to duty.
normal.cn: 在计算领域，activate 解锁产品；在军事领域，它让预备役部队转入现役。

abstract.en: Picture a dusty machine in a dark workshop, then a switch clicks and the belt begins to turn.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗车间里一台落灰的机器，开关一响，传送带开始转动。

abstract.en: Picture a gene lying folded and silent, then a protein arrives and it begins to read.
abstract.cn: 想象一个折叠静默的基因，一种蛋白质到来后它开始读取。

abstract.en: Picture a whole city's water system coming alive valve by valve.
abstract.cn: 想象整座城市的水系统一个阀门接一个阀门地活起来。

examples.en: The technician pressed the switch to activate the new system.
examples.cn: 技术员按下开关，让新系统开始运转。

examples.en: The governor activated the national guard after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，州长调动国民警卫队进入现役。

examples.en: You must activate the program before the trial period ends.
examples.cn: 你必须在试用期结束前激活这个程序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维特」——阿克一提开关，机器就活了起来

root: 拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」→ actus / activus「活跃的」→ 中世纪拉丁语 activare「使活动」→ 英语 activate。PIE *ag-「驱动、做」一般认为成立，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of activate all turn a dormant thing on: a device, a plan, a chemical, a gene, a unit, software, a facility, or demand.
sensesIntro.cn: activate 的八个义项都把一个沉睡之物打开：设备、计划、化学品、基因、部队、软件、设施或需求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand turns a switch and a sleeping machine begins to move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拨动开关，沉睡的机器开始运动。

branches.en: THE SWITCH: a device or a plan moves from idle to running.
branches.cn: 开关线：设备或计划从闲置转入运行。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: heat, a catalyst or a protein wakes a chemical or a gene.
branches.cn: 物质线：热量、催化剂或蛋白质唤醒化学品或基因。

branches.en: THE FORCE: a reserve unit is called from storage into active duty.
branches.cn: 部队线：预备役被从储备状态调入现役。

branches.en: THE INSTALLATION: software and public facilities are unlocked and brought online.
branches.cn: 安装线：软件与公共设施被解锁并接入运行。

branches.en: THE MARKET: demand that was asleep is set in motion.
branches.cn: 市场线：沉睡的需求被带动起来。

intro.en: Activate is a Latin doing-root with an adjective and a verb suffix, the same material as action and actor.
intro.cn: activate 是拉丁语「做」词根加形容词与动词词尾，与 action、actor 的材料相同。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, actus and activus are recorded; the medieval verb activare is also attested, though its earliest date is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere、actus 与 activus 均有记录；中世纪动词 activare 也有文献可证，但确切年代不确定。

items.example: The verb is the doing core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中「做」的核心。
这个分词变成英语的 act。
这个形容词变成英语的 active。

items.example: The verb is the model for English activate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语 activate 的模板。

definition_zh: 实际的；真实的；当前的；事实上的
definition_en: existing in fact rather than only in thought or expectation
core_image: 账本左边写着预算，右边写着真正花出去的钱
scene: 账目上写着预算，真正花出去的钱却比预算多出许多。The actual cost of the repair was far higher than the estimate.
sceneCN: 这里 actual 是「实际的」（第 5 个义项：实际发生的成本或金额）；句意为这次维修的实际花费远高于估算。

pos.zh: 形容词：实际的；真实的；当前的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「实际上；其实」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「现实性；实际情况」
由形容词加动词后缀构成，义为「实现；使成为现实」
由 actualize 加名词后缀构成，义为「实现；现实化」

senses.title: Real rather than imagined
senses.definition: existing in fact, not only in thought, plans, or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 确实存在，而非只存在于想法、计划或想象中
senses.example: The story is based on actual events in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事以村里真实发生过的事件为基础。
senses.why: Actualis comes from actus, an act: what is actual is what has actually been done or has happened.
senses.whyCN: actualis 来自 actus「行为」：实际的就是确实做过或发生过的东西。

senses.title: Current or present
senses.definition: existing or happening now, as opposed to an earlier or later state
senses.definitionCN: 现在存在或发生的，相对于更早或更晚的状态
senses.example: The actual position of the ship was twenty miles north of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船的当前位置在计划位置以北二十英里。
senses.why: What is in act at this moment is what is present, so actual can mark the current state.
senses.whyCN: 此刻正在「行动中」的东西就是当下的东西，因此 actual 可以标记当前状态。

senses.title: Factual and precise
senses.definition: based on facts and exact detail rather than on a general impression
senses.definitionCN: 以事实与确切细节为依据，而非依据笼统印象
senses.example: We need the actual figures, not a rough estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要确切数字，而不是粗略估计。
senses.why: The word pulls attention from appearance to the recorded act or number.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把注意力从表面印象拉向被记录下来的行为或数字。

senses.title: Practical rather than theoretical
senses.definition: measured or tested in real conditions rather than worked out on paper
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下测量或检验，而非只在纸面上推算
senses.example: The actual performance of the engine differed from the model.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机的实际表现与模型不符。
senses.why: Theory describes what might happen; the act describes what did happen.
senses.whyCN: 理论描述可能发生的事，行为则描述已经发生的事。

senses.title: The real amount or cost
senses.definition: the amount that is really paid or produced, as opposed to a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 真正支付或产生的数额，相对于预测值
senses.example: The actual cost of the repair was far higher than the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修的实际花费远高于估算。
senses.why: Money, time and output all have a planned figure and a acted figure, and actual picks the second.
senses.whyCN: 金钱、时间与产量都有计划数字与实际数字，actual 选的是后者。

senses.title: In actual fact
senses.definition: used in the phrase in actual fact to correct an assumption or add emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in actual fact，纠正一个假设或加强语气
senses.example: In actual fact, the meeting had already been cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 事实上，会议早已取消。
senses.why: The phrase turns the listener from what was assumed to what actually happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把听者从假设的情况转到真正发生的情况。

senses.title: Actual versus potential
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing what exists now rather than what could exist
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，描述现在存在的东西，相对于可能存在的东西
senses.example: The philosopher asked whether the plan was actual or only potential.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家追问该计划是现实的，还是仅仅潜在的。
senses.why: The pair actual and potential separates what is in act from what is merely able to be.
senses.whyCN: actual 与 potential 这对词区分「已在行动中」的东西与「仅仅可能」的东西。

senses.title: Actual damage in law
senses.definition: in law, damage that has really occurred, as distinct from damage that is only feared or threatened
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，已经真正发生的损害，区别于仅被担心或威胁的损害
senses.example: The court awarded compensation for actual damage, not for future risk.
senses.exampleCN: 法院只对实际损害判给赔偿，而不对未来风险判赔。
senses.why: Law must separate harm that happened from harm that might happen, and actual marks the first.
senses.whyCN: 法律必须区分已发生的损害与可能发生的损害，actual 标记前者。

intro.en: Actual comes from the Latin word for an act, and its modern sense of 'real' grew from 'what has been done'.
intro.cn: actual 来自拉丁语表示「行为」的词，现代「真实的」义从「已经做出的」发展而来。

items.en: *ag- is generally reconstructed as 'to drive, do'; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ag- 表示「驱动、做」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: agere meant 'to do, act', the source of actus and of the whole family.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、行动」，是 actus 与整个词族的来源。

items.en: actus meant 'a doing, an act, a driving'; it passed into English as act.
items.cn: actus 意为「行为、举动、驱动」，进入英语成为 act。

items.en: actualis meant 'relating to action or practice', not yet 'real' as in modern English.
items.cn: actualis 意为「与行动或实践有关的」，当时还没有现代英语「真实的」义。

items.en: Old French actuel carried the word toward English with senses of active and present.
items.cn: 古法语 actuel 把这个词带向英语，带有「活动的、当下的」含义。

items.en: English actual is recorded in the fourteenth century; the modern sense of real develops later, and exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 actual 在十四世纪已有记录；现代「真实的」义后来才发展出来，确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agere family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is true or present.
note.cn: 形近组收 agere 词族；近义组收表示真实或当下的形容词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in fact, or used to correct a mistaken assumption.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上」，或用于纠正错误假设。

entries.definition: The state of being real or the facts of a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实性、实际情况」，指真实存在的状态或事情的真实状况。

entries.definition: To make a plan or possibility real.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现」，把计划或可能性变成现实。

entries.definition: A deed, or to do something; the shortest member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「行为；行动」，是词族中最短的一个。

entries.definition: The process of doing something, or a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动、行为」，指做某事的过程或一件行为。

entries.definition: Existing in the physical world, not imagined or invented.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真实的」，存在于现实世界，而非想象或虚构。

entries.definition: Truly what it claims to be, not fake or copied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「真正的」，确实是所声称的东西，而非伪造或仿制。

entries.definition: Based on facts and containing no invention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「事实的」，以事实为依据，不含虚构。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「当前的」，现在正在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: Specific and real rather than general or abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「具体的」，明确而真实，而非笼统或抽象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the act root, the planned-versus-real contrast, and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 act 词根、计划与真实的对照，以及这个词出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: actus is 'an act': actual is what has actually been done, not what was planned.
normal.cn: actus 是「行为」：actual 是真正做过的事，而不是计划中的事。

normal.en: The same root gives act, action, actor and agenda, all about doing.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 act、action、actor、agenda，全都与「做」有关。

normal.en: In actual fact is the phrase that corrects an assumption and points to what happened.
normal.cn: in actual fact 是用来纠正假设、指向真实情况的短语。

normal.en: Actual and potential are a philosophical pair: one is in act, the other only possible.
normal.cn: actual 与 potential 是哲学上的一对：一个已在行动中，另一个只是可能。

normal.en: Actually is not the same as currently; it means in truth, often to contradict.
normal.cn: actually 不等于 currently；它的意思是「实际上」，常用于反驳。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with a forecast on the left page and the real figures on the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账本，左页是预测，右页是真实数字。

abstract.en: Picture a map route and the muddy footprints that show where someone really walked.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上的一条路线，以及显示某人真正走过哪里的泥脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a scale model beside the full-size object it represents.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按比例缩小的模型，旁边放着它所代表的实物。

examples.en: The actual cost of the repair was far higher than the estimate.
examples.cn: 这次维修的实际花费远高于估算。

examples.en: The story is based on actual events in the village.
examples.cn: 这个故事以村里真实发生过的事件为基础。

examples.en: In actual fact, the meeting had already been cancelled.
examples.cn: 事实上，会议早已取消。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of actual all contrast what is real with what is imagined, planned, theoretical, feared or merely possible.
sensesIntro.cn: actual 的八个义项都把真实之物与想象、计划、理论、担忧或仅仅可能之物相对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forecast sheet and a receipt are laid side by side, and the receipt wins.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张预测单与一张收据并排放着，收据才是真的。

branches.en: THE FACT: what is actual has really happened, unlike a story or a guess.
branches.cn: 事实线：实际之物确实发生过，不同于故事或猜测。

branches.en: THE PRESENT: the state in act now is the current state.
branches.cn: 当下线：此刻正在行动中的状态就是当前状态。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: exact figures and real costs replace estimates.
branches.cn: 数字线：确切数字与实际成本取代估算。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: performance in real conditions is set against theory and potential.
branches.cn: 实践线：真实条件下的表现与理论、潜能相对照。

branches.en: THE EMPHASIS: in actual fact and in law, the word separates what happened from what was assumed or feared.
branches.cn: 强调线：在 in actual fact 与法律用法中，这个词区分已发生之事与假设或担忧之事。

intro.en: Actual is a Latin act-word with an adjective ending; the same stem runs through act, action and agenda.
intro.cn: actual 是拉丁语「行为」词加形容词词尾；同一词干贯穿 act、action 与 agenda。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, actus and actualis are recorded, so the family is documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere、actus 与 actualis 均有记录，这个词族有文献可证，不属于重构。

definition_en: the act of obtaining something, the thing obtained, or the purchase of a company
core_image: 合同签字后，钥匙从一只手换到另一只手
scene: 谈判桌上两份文件推过来，双方代表在末尾签下名字，随后握手。The acquisition of the smaller firm closed in June.
sceneCN: 这里 acquisition 是「收购」（第 3 个义项：买下一家公司）；句意为对那家较小公司的收购在六月完成。

senses.title: The act of obtaining
senses.definition: the act or process of getting something
senses.definitionCN: 取得某物的行为或过程
senses.example: The acquisition of new skills takes steady practice.
senses.exampleCN: 获得新技能需要稳定练习。
senses.why: The -sition ending names the action, so acquisition is the getting rather than the thing got.
senses.whyCN: -sition 后缀标记行为，因此 acquisition 指「取得」这个动作，而非所得之物。

senses.title: Something obtained
senses.definition: a thing that has been obtained, often added to a collection
senses.definitionCN: 获得之物，常指收藏中新添的一件
senses.example: The museum announced its latest acquisition.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆公布了最新入藏的藏品。
senses.why: Museums and libraries use the noun for the object itself, turning the process into a catalogue entry.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与图书馆用这个名词指物品本身，把过程变成一条馆藏记录。

senses.title: The purchase of a company
senses.definition: the buying of a company or business
senses.definitionCN: 买下一家公司或业务
senses.example: The acquisition of the smaller firm closed in June.
senses.exampleCN: 对那家较小公司的收购在六月完成。
senses.why: Business borrowed the legal sense of 'coming to possess', and the deal became the word.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用了「取得占有」的法律含义，交易本身就成了这个词。

intro.cn: acquisition 是 acquire 的名词形式，来自拉丁语 acquisitio，由 acquirere（额外取得）构成。

items.en: quaerere meant 'to seek', the root behind the verb.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求」，是动词背后的词根。

items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外取得」。

items.en: acquisitio named the act of gaining.

items.en: English acquisition first meant the act of obtaining.
items.cn: 英语 acquisition 最初指获得的行为。

items.cn: 现代用法增加了语言习得与公司收购。

note.cn: 第一组收动词与形容词词族；第二组收表示获得与买下的词。

core_image: 法槌落下，被告席上的人被解开手铐
scene: 庭审持续了三天，陪审团反复核对证据。The acquittal came after the key witness changed his story.

senses.definitionCN: 法庭正式判定被告无罪
senses.example: The acquittal came after the key witness changed his story.
senses.exampleCN: 关键证人改口之后，无罪判决才出现。

senses.whyCN: 古法语 acquiter 意为「清偿债务」，法律借用了这个意象：罪名被清掉。

senses.title: Release from a duty or debt
senses.definition: the act of freeing someone from a debt or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免于债务或义务的行为
senses.example: The records note the acquittal of the old debt.
senses.exampleCN: 记录中注明了旧债的清偿。

senses.whyCN: 法律义从财务义生长而来；acquit 最初是「结清账目」。

senses.definition: a thing added to help a main thing but not needed for it to exist
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助主体而添加、但主体缺它也能存在的东西
senses.example: The appendix serves as an adjunct to the main report.
senses.exampleCN: 附录是主报告的附属部分。
senses.why: adjungere is 'to join to', and an adjunct is joined to a main body without becoming its core.
senses.whyCN: adjungere 意为「接上去」，adjunct 被接到主体上，却不会变成主体的核心。

senses.title: An optional grammatical element
senses.definition: a sentence element that adds information but can be removed without breaking the grammar
senses.definitionCN: 为主要结构补充信息、去掉后语法仍成立的句子成分
senses.example: The teacher marked the time phrase as an adjunct to the main clause.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把时间短语标为主句的附加成分。
senses.why: Grammar separates the core clause from what is merely joined on to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法把核心小句与仅仅接上去的成分区分开来。

senses.title: A junior academic post
senses.definition: a teaching or research post attached to a department on a part-time or temporary basis
senses.definitionCN: 以兼职或临时方式挂靠在某个院系的教学或研究职位
senses.example: She taught as an adjunct at the university for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这所大学做了两年兼职教师。
senses.why: The post is attached to the department without being part of its permanent core.
senses.whyCN: 这个职位挂在院系上，却不属于其永久核心。

senses.title: A non-essential property in philosophy
senses.definition: a property that a thing may have or lose without ceasing to be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 某物可以拥有或失去、却不因此改变其本质的属性
senses.example: Colour is treated as an adjunct of the object, not its essence.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色被视为物体的偶性，而非其本质。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the joined-on image for qualities that come and go.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用「接上去」的意象，指那些来来去去的性质。

senses.title: A supporting medical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment added to the main therapy to improve its effect
senses.definitionCN: 加在主要疗法之上以增强疗效的治疗
senses.example: The drug is used as an adjunct to surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药被用作手术的辅助治疗。
senses.why: The main therapy carries the cure, and the adjunct is joined on to help it work better.
senses.whyCN: 主要疗法承担治愈，辅助治疗接上去帮它更好地发挥作用。

senses.title: A person who assists
senses.definition: in older usage, a person who helps another in a task
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指在任务中帮助另一个人的助手
senses.example: The clerk worked as an adjunct to the chief magistrate.
senses.exampleCN: 这名书记员担任首席治安官的助手。
senses.why: A helper is joined to the main office-holder in the same way as a small part to a body.
senses.whyCN: 助手像一个小部件接在主体上一样，接在主职者身边。

senses.title: An attached condition
senses.definition: a condition or qualification attached to an agreement or a statement
senses.definitionCN: 附加在协议或声明上的条件或限定
senses.example: The permit came with an adjunct requiring monthly reports.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证附带一项要求每月报告的条件。
senses.why: A condition is joined to the main arrangement without replacing it.
senses.whyCN: 条件被接到主要安排上，而不取代它。

senses.title: A physically attached part
senses.definition: a part fixed to a larger structure to extend its function
senses.definitionCN: 固定在较大结构上、用以扩展其功能的部件
senses.example: The pump is an adjunct to the main irrigation line.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵是主灌溉管线的附属部件。
senses.why: The most literal sense is a piece joined on to a larger machine or building.
senses.whyCN: 最字面的义项就是接在较大机器或建筑上的部件。

intro.en: Adjunct comes from the Latin verb for joining one thing to another, the same root as junction.
intro.cn: adjunct 来自表示「把一物接到另一物」的拉丁语动词，与 junction 同根。

items.en: jungere meant 'to join, yoke', the source of junction, join and junta.
items.cn: jungere 意为「连接、套上轭」，是 junction、join 与 junta 的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus jungere formed adjungere, 'to join to, attach'.
items.cn: ad- 表示「向」，与 jungere 构成 adjungere，意为「接上、附加」。

items.en: The participle adjunctus meant 'joined to', and it became the English noun.
items.cn: 分词 adjunctus 意为「被接上的」，后来成为英语名词。

items.en: The noun adjunctio named the act of adding something on.
items.cn: 名词 adjunctio 指把某物附加上去的行为。

items.en: English adjunct is recorded in the fifteenth century; the grammatical and academic senses develop later, with exact dates uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 adjunct 在十五世纪已有记录；语法义与学术义后来才发展，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from grammar and medicine to part-time academic posts and attached parts.
items.cn: 现代用法从语法、医学延伸到兼职学术职位与附属部件。

examples.en: It took her months to adapt to the new climate.
examples.cn: 她花了几个月才适应新气候。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达普特」——把旧东西改到合身，就是适应或改编。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ aptare（使合适）→ adaptare；核心义是「改动以合身」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from fitting a new environment, to modifying something for a new use.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从适应新环境，走到为新的用途改动某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old piece rebuilt for a smaller room
core.cn: 核心意象：旧物被重装以适合更小的房间

branches.en: To change so as to work in a new situation.
branches.cn: 为在新环境运作而改变。

branches.en: To modify something for a different use.
branches.cn: 改动某物以适合另一种用途。

branches.en: Living things and designed things both 'fit' anew.
branches.cn: 生物与设计物都要重新「合身」。

branches.en: Adjust is the small version of adapt.
branches.cn: adjust 是 adapt 的小幅版本。

branches.en: Both senses keep the Latin image of fitting.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留拉丁语「合身」意象。

intro.en: The verb joins the prefix ad- (to) with the fit root apt- and the verb ending -t, and its family adds noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: 这个动词把前缀 ad-（向）与「合身」词根 apt- 及动词词尾 -t 结合，词族另加名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin adaptare is the direct ancestor, recorded here with aptare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adaptare 是直接祖先，这里连同 aptare 一并记录。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「适应；改编」
形容词，义为「能适应的」

definition_zh: 过道；走道；侧廊；婚礼通道
definition_en: a passage between rows of seats, shelves, or pews, or the route a bride walks at a wedding
core_image: 两排座位之间留出一条窄路，人沿它向前走
scene: 婚礼开始前，伴娘沿着座位之间的通道慢慢往前走。Before the ceremony, the bridesmaid walked slowly up the aisle between the pews.
sceneCN: 这里 aisle 是「婚礼通道」（第 4 个义项：婚礼上通向圣坛的走道）；句意为仪式开始前，伴娘沿着座椅之间的通道慢慢向前走。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有侧廊的」
由本词加否定后缀构成，义为「无侧廊的」

senses.title: A passage between seats
senses.definition: a narrow walkway between rows of seats in a theatre, plane, or hall
senses.definitionCN: 剧院、飞机或大厅中两排座位之间的窄走道
senses.example: He chose an aisle seat so he could stretch his legs.
senses.exampleCN: 他选了靠过道的座位，好伸展双腿。
senses.why: The word's oldest surviving sense is the narrow route beside the seating.
senses.whyCN: 这个词现存最古老的义项就是座位旁的一条窄路。

senses.title: A supermarket aisle
senses.definition: the space between shelves in a shop where customers walk
senses.definitionCN: 商店中货架之间供顾客行走的空间
senses.example: The pasta is in the third aisle on the left.
senses.exampleCN: 意大利面在左边第三条货道。
senses.why: Shops arrange goods in rows, and the spaces between rows take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 商店把商品排成行，行与行之间的空间也使用同一个名称。

senses.title: A church side aisle
senses.definition: a long passage alongside the nave of a church
senses.definitionCN: 教堂中殿旁边的一条长通道
senses.example: The old church had a narrow aisle on each side.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老教堂两侧各有一条窄侧廊。
senses.why: Church architecture used the word for the wings beside the main body, from the Latin word for wing.
senses.whyCN: 教堂建筑用这个词指主体两旁的部分，源自拉丁语「翼」。

senses.title: The wedding route
senses.definition: the passage a bride walks along to reach the altar
senses.definitionCN: 新娘走向圣坛时所经的通道
senses.example: The bridesmaid walked slowly up the aisle between the pews.
senses.exampleCN: 伴娘沿着座椅之间的通道慢慢向前走。
senses.why: The church aisle became the fixed stage of the wedding ceremony, and the phrase kept the word.
senses.whyCN: 教堂走道成为婚礼仪式的固定舞台，短语把这个词保留下来。

senses.title: Across the political aisle
senses.definition: in politics, cooperation between parties that sit on opposite sides of a chamber
senses.definitionCN: 在政治中，议事厅两侧不同党派之间的合作
senses.example: The bill passed with support from across the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 该法案在跨党派支持下通过。
senses.why: Seating in a legislature is divided by a central aisle, so the passage becomes a metaphor for party division.
senses.whyCN: 立法机构的座位被中央走道分开，这条走道于是成为党派分歧的隐喻。

senses.title: A narrow building passage
senses.definition: a long narrow passage inside a large building
senses.definitionCN: 大型建筑内部的一条狭长通道
senses.example: A side aisle led from the hall to the service door.
senses.exampleCN: 一条侧通道从大厅通向后勤门。
senses.why: Any long strip between two structures can be called an aisle.
senses.whyCN: 两座结构之间的任何长条空间都可以叫 aisle。

senses.title: A space between racks
senses.definition: the gap between storage racks in a warehouse
senses.definitionCN: 仓库中储货架之间的空隙
senses.example: The forklift needed a wider aisle to turn.
senses.exampleCN: 叉车需要更宽的货道才能转弯。
senses.why: Warehouse layout repeats the shop pattern at a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 仓库布局在更大尺度上重复了商店的模式。

senses.title: The wedding as a whole
senses.definition: by metonymy, the marriage ceremony itself in the phrase walk down the aisle
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 walk down the aisle 中，以通道转指婚礼仪式本身
senses.example: They walked down the aisle after ten years together.
senses.exampleCN: 相处十年后，他们走上了婚礼通道。
senses.why: The route stands for the event, a common metonymy in English.
senses.whyCN: 路线转指事件，这是英语中常见的转喻。

intro.en: Aisle began as a word for a wing and gained its modern spelling by confusion with isle.
intro.cn: aisle 最初指「翼」，现代拼写是因与 isle 混淆而加上字母 s。

items.en: ala meant 'wing', and it also gave English alar and alate.
items.cn: ala 意为「翼」，还给出英语的 alar 与 alate。

items.en: Old French aile meant 'wing, flank', and it was used for the side parts of a church.
items.cn: 古法语 aile 意为「翼、侧面」，被用来指教堂的侧部。

items.en: Middle English ile named the side passage of a church, still without an s.
items.cn: 中古英语 ile 指教堂的侧廊，当时仍没有字母 s。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the spelling was altered to aisle by association with isle, a false etymological link.
items.cn: 十六世纪时，受 isle 影响，拼写被改成 aisle，这是一种错误的词源联想。

items.en: The new spelling spread and also covered passages between seats and shelves.
items.cn: 新拼写传播开来，也扩展到座位与货架之间的通道。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from churches and theatres to supermarkets, aircraft and legislatures.
items.cn: 现代用法从教堂、剧院延伸到超市、飞机与立法机构。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the homophone isle and related forms; the near-meaning group gathers passage words.
note.cn: 形近组收同音词 isle 及相关形式；近义组收表示通道的词。

entries.definition: An island, especially a small one; it sounds exactly like aisle but comes from Latin insula.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小岛」；与 aisle 同音，但来自拉丁语 insula。

entries.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water; its spelling was also influenced by isle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「岛」，被水环绕的陆地；拼写也受 isle 影响。

entries.definition: Having one or more aisles, used of a church.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有侧廊的」，用于描述教堂。

entries.definition: Having no aisle.
A rare word for a passage that serves as an aisle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，罕见用法，义为「过道式通道」。

entries.definition: A route through or between buildings or rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道」，穿过或位于建筑、房间之间的路线。

entries.definition: A long narrow passage in a building or a train.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「走廊」，建筑或火车中的狭长通道。

entries.definition: A passage for people to walk through, especially on a ship or between seats.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道、舷梯」，供人行走的通道，尤指船上或座位之间。

entries.definition: A path built for walking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「步道」，为行走而建的路径。

entries.definition: A way through something, or the act of moving through.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通道；通过」，穿过某物的路，或通过的行为。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the false isle link, the church-wing origin, and the rows-and-gap image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用与 isle 的错误联系、教堂侧翼的来源，以及「一排排与空隙」的意象。

normal.en: Think of rows of seats with one gap: that gap is the aisle.
normal.cn: 想象一排排座位中间留出一个空隙，那个空隙就是 aisle。

normal.en: The s in aisle is silent, exactly as in isle.
normal.cn: aisle 里的 s 不发音，与 isle 完全一样。

normal.en: The spelling s was added by mistake, linking the word to isle; the older form was ile.
normal.cn: 拼写中的 s 是错误添加的，把它与 isle 联系起来；更早的形式是 ile。

normal.en: Aisle seat is the common phrase that keeps the word in daily use.
normal.cn: aisle seat 是让这个词在日常中存活的常见搭配。

normal.en: Walk down the aisle is a metonymy for getting married.
normal.cn: walk down the aisle 是「结婚」的转喻。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow strip of floor between two rows of chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象两排椅子之间一条窄窄的地面。

abstract.en: Picture a bride moving slowly toward an altar at the end of a long passage.
abstract.cn: 想象新娘沿着一条长通道缓缓走向圣坛。

abstract.en: Picture a legislature split into two sides by a central walkway.
abstract.cn: 想象立法机构被中央走道分成两侧。

examples.en: The bridesmaid walked slowly up the aisle between the pews.
examples.cn: 伴娘沿着座椅之间的通道慢慢向前走。

examples.en: He chose an aisle seat so he could stretch his legs.
examples.cn: 他选了靠过道的座位，好伸展双腿。

examples.en: The bill passed with support from across the aisle.
examples.cn: 该法案在跨党派支持下通过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾尔」——艾尔沿着两排椅子中间那条窄路往前走

root: 拉丁语 ala「翼」→ 古法语 aile「翼、侧面」→ 中古英语 ile「教堂侧廊」；十六世纪受 isle 影响误加字母 s，成为 aisle，并扩展到座位与货架之间的通道。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of aisle all describe a narrow route between two rows, from church wings to supermarket shelves, wedding processions and legislative divisions.
sensesIntro.cn: aisle 的八个义项都描述两排之间的一条窄路，从教堂侧翼到超市货架、婚礼队列与立法机构的分席。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip of floor between two rows of chairs.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排椅子之间一条窄窄的地面。

branches.en: THE ROWS: seats, shelves and racks create the gap people walk through.
branches.cn: 成排线：座位、货架与储架形成供人穿行的空隙。

branches.en: THE SHOP: retail aisles organise goods into walkable lanes.
branches.cn: 商店线：零售货道把商品排成可行走的通道。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: church wings and long side passages keep the architectural sense.
branches.cn: 建筑线：教堂侧翼与长侧通道保留建筑义。

branches.en: THE WEDDING: the church route becomes the stage of the ceremony and then the ceremony itself.
branches.cn: 婚礼线：教堂路线成为仪式舞台，进而转指仪式本身。

branches.en: THE POLITICS: the central walkway becomes a metaphor for party division.
branches.cn: 政治线：中央走道成为党派分歧的隐喻。

intro.en: Aisle comes from a Latin wing word through French, with English adjective endings added later.
intro.cn: aisle 由拉丁语「翼」这个词经法语传来，后来加上英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ala and Old French aile are recorded; the modern spelling is a documented later alteration, not an inherited form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ala 与古法语 aile 均有记录；现代拼写是有文献可查的后期改动，而非继承形式。

items.example: The Latin noun is the remote source.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁语名词是远源。

items.example: The French noun named church side parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词指教堂的侧部。

items.example: The older English form had no s.
items.exampleCN: 较早的英语形式没有字母 s。

items.example: The respelled form is the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 改拼后的形式就是现代词。

definition_zh: 适应能力；适应性；可改造性
definition_en: the capacity to change in order to fit new conditions or purposes
core_image: 一把能变形的椅子，坐、躺、叠都行
scene: 同一间小屋，白天是办公室，晚上收起桌面就成了卧室。The adaptability of the design saved both space and money.
sceneCN: 这里 adaptability 是「适应性、可变通性」（第 2 个义项：设计或系统能被改作他用）；句意为这种设计的适应性既省空间又省钱。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「能适应的」
动词，义为「适应」
名词，义为「适应；改编」

senses.title: Capacity to adjust
senses.definition: the ability to change so as to fit new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为适合新环境而改变的能力
senses.example: Children show great adaptability in a new school.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在新学校表现出很强的适应能力。
senses.why: -ability names a capacity, so adaptability is the power behind the act of adapting.
senses.whyCN: -ability 标记能力，因此 adaptability 是 adapting 背后的力量。

senses.title: Capacity to be reworked
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to modify for another use
senses.definitionCN: 容易被改作他用的性质
senses.example: The adaptability of the design saved both space and money.
senses.exampleCN: 这种设计的适应性既省空间又省钱。
senses.why: Designers use the noun for objects too: a good chair or app can be reshaped without loss.
senses.whyCN: 设计师也用这个名词指物品：好的椅子或应用能被重新改造而不受损。

intro.en: Adaptability is adaptable plus -ity, tracing back through adapt to Latin aptus, 'fit'.
intro.cn: adaptability 是 adaptable 加 -ity，经 adapt 追溯到拉丁语 aptus（合适的）。

items.en: aptus meant 'fit, suited'.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的」。

items.en: adaptare meant 'to fit to'.
items.cn: adaptare 意为「使适合」。

items.en: English adapt entered use in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语 adapt 在十七世纪进入使用。

items.en: the ending -able marks what can be done.
items.cn: -able 后缀标记可被做到。

items.en: the ending -ity turns the adjective into a capacity.
items.cn: -ity 后缀把形容词变成能力。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and verb family; the second gathers nouns of flexible capacity.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与动词词族；第二组收表示灵活能力的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'able to adjust'.
The verb meaning 'to fit or modify'.
The noun for the process or the reworked thing.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多才多艺；多功能」

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ability capacity and the foldable chair; the abstract hooks picture one room used two ways.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -ability 的能力义与折叠椅；抽象记忆点想象一间房两种用法。

normal.en: Adaptability is the -ity capacity behind adaptable.
normal.cn: adaptability 是 adaptable 背后的 -ity 能力。

normal.en: Adaptability to change is the key phrase.
normal.cn: adaptability to change 是关键说法。

normal.en: The adjective is adaptable, the verb adapt.
normal.cn: 形容词是 adaptable，动词是 adapt。

normal.en: High adaptability means quick recovery.
normal.cn: high adaptability 指快速恢复。

normal.en: A system's adaptability is its reworkable quality.
normal.cn: 系统的 adaptability 指可改造性。

abstract.en: Picture a chair that sits, reclines, and folds.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能坐、能躺、能折的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a room that is office by day and bedroom by night.
abstract.cn: 想象一间白天办公、晚上当卧室的房。

abstract.en: Picture a plant surviving both drought and flood.
abstract.cn: 想象植物旱涝都能存活。

examples.en: Children show great adaptability in a new school.
examples.cn: 孩子在新学校表现出很强的适应能力。

examples.en: The adaptability of the design saved both space and money.
examples.cn: 这种设计的适应性既省空间又省钱。

examples.en: Employers value adaptability to change.
examples.cn: 雇主看重对变化的适应能力。

sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从调整能力，走到可被改造的性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair that sits, reclines, and folds
core.cn: 核心意象：一把能坐能躺能折的椅子

branches.en: The ability to adjust to new conditions.
branches.cn: 适应新环境的能力。

branches.en: The quality of being easily reworked.
branches.cn: 容易被改造的性质。

branches.en: Living things and products share this capacity.
branches.cn: 生物与产品共享这种能力。

branches.en: Flexibility is the physical face of adaptability.
branches.cn: 灵活性是适应性的物理面貌。

intro.en: The noun joins adaptable with the capacity ending -ity, and its family keeps adjective, verb, and process noun.
intro.cn: 这个名词把 adaptable 与表能力的后缀 -ity 结合，词族保留形容词、动词与过程名词。

scene: 野外考察队只带一套工具，遇到缺绳、缺支架就用备用件拼。The adaptable shelter worked in wind, rain, and snow.
sceneCN: 这里 adaptable 是「能适应的、可变通的」（第 1 个义项：能随环境改变而正常工作）；句意为这种可变的庇护所在风、雨、雪里都能用。

senses.title: Able to adjust
senses.definition: able to change so as to work well in new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 能改变以在新环境中良好运作
senses.example: The adaptable shelter worked in wind, rain, and snow.
senses.exampleCN: 这种可变的庇护所在风、雨、雪里都能用。
senses.why: -able marks the ability, so adaptable describes whoever or whatever can complete the act of adapting.
senses.whyCN: -able 标记能力，因此 adaptable 描述能完成 adapting 这个动作的人或物。

senses.title: Able to be modified
senses.definition: able to be changed for a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: 能被改动以适合别的用途
senses.example: The adaptable design serves both a desk and a bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种可改造的设计既能当书桌也能当床。
senses.why: The same ending can point outward: an object is adaptable when a user can reshape it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也可指向外部：一件物品能被使用者改造，就是 adaptable。

senses.title: Dependence on a substance

senses.title: Strong devotion to an activity

senses.title: Extra in amount
senses.definition: added to what already exists, often increasing a cost or amount

senses.title: Further or supplementary

definition_en: the feeling of finding something funny, or an activity or device that entertains people
core_image: 旋转木马转起来，孩子的笑声跟着一起转
scene: 孩子坐上旋转木马，一圈又一圈，笑得停不下来。The child rode the carousel round and round, laughing with amusement.
sceneCN: 这里 amusement 是「觉得好笑、乐趣」（第 2 个义项：被某事逗乐的感觉）；句意为孩子坐着旋转木马一圈圈地转，笑得停不下来。

pos.zh: 名词：娱乐；消遣；乐趣；游乐设施

derivatives.zh: 由法语动词借入，义为「逗乐；使消遣」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「好笑的；有趣的」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「被逗乐的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「有趣地；好笑地」

senses.title: Entertainment as an activity
senses.definition: an activity that people do for enjoyment rather than work
senses.definitionCN: 人们为享乐而非工作进行的活动
senses.example: The town offers few amusements for teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇子给青少年的娱乐活动很少。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that diverts attention away from work and worry.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指把人注意力从工作与忧虑上引开的东西。

senses.title: The feeling of being amused
senses.definition: the pleasant feeling produced by something funny or lightly entertaining
senses.definitionCN: 由好笑或轻松有趣的事物带来的愉快感觉
senses.example: The child rode the carousel round and round, laughing with amusement.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子坐着旋转木马一圈圈地转，笑得停不下来。
senses.why: This is the inward sense: the laugh happens inside before it becomes an activity.
senses.whyCN: 这是向内的义项：笑声先在内心发生，之后才变成活动。

senses.title: A hobby or pastime
senses.definition: a leisure interest that fills spare time pleasantly
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地填满空闲时间的消遣兴趣
senses.example: Gardening was his chief amusement after retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是他退休后的主要消遣。
senses.why: Anything that occupies idle time pleasantly can be called an amusement.
senses.whyCN: 任何能愉快占据空闲时间的事物都可称作 amusement。

senses.title: A fairground ride
senses.definition: a mechanical ride or attraction in a funfair or amusement park
senses.definitionCN: 游乐场或主题公园里的机械游乐设施
senses.example: The park added a new water amusement last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 公园去年夏天新增了一项水上娱乐设施。
senses.why: The word shifted from the feeling to the machines that produce it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从感觉转向了生产这种感觉的机器。

senses.title: The entertainment industry
senses.definition: the business of providing shows, games, and leisure attractions
senses.definitionCN: 提供演出、游戏与休闲项目的行业
senses.example: He works in amusement and leisure services.
senses.exampleCN: 他在娱乐与休闲服务业工作。
senses.why: An abstract noun can name a whole commercial sector.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词可以指整个商业部门。

senses.title: The act of amusing someone
senses.definition: something done to make another person laugh or smile
senses.definitionCN: 为让别人发笑或微笑而做的事
senses.example: His jokes were a constant amusement to the office.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话是办公室里持续不断的乐子。
senses.why: The noun can name the causing act, not only the feeling it produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指「逗」的行为，而不只是它带来的感觉。

senses.title: A light diversion
senses.definition: a small game, puzzle, or light entertainment used to pass time
senses.definitionCN: 用来打发时间的小游戏、谜题或轻松娱乐品
senses.example: The magazine is a harmless amusement for a train journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志是火车旅途上无害的消遣。
senses.why: Amusement often implies lightness, something that does not demand serious effort.
senses.whyCN: amusement 常含「轻」的意思：不要求认真投入的东西。

senses.title: Amusement at another's misfortune
senses.titleCN: 对他人的不幸感到兴味
senses.definition: a detached or ironic interest in something odd or unfortunate
senses.definitionCN: 对古怪或不幸之事持有的超然、带讽意的兴趣
senses.example: She watched the argument with quiet amusement.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着淡淡的兴味看着这场争吵。
senses.why: The feeling can be cool rather than warm, closer to wry interest than laughter.
senses.whyCN: 这种感受可以是冷的而非热的，更接近苦笑式的兴味，而不是大笑。

intro.en: Amusement comes from French, and its root first meant to stare or gape rather than to laugh.
intro.cn: amusement 来自法语，其词根最初意为「盯着看、发呆」，而非「笑」。

items.en: muser meant 'to meditate, muse, stare idly'.
items.cn: muser 意为「沉思、出神、闲看」。

items.en: amuser meant 'to divert, occupy pleasantly', literally to set someone musing.
items.cn: amuser 意为「使分心、使愉快地消磨」，字面是「让人出神」。

items.en: The noun amusement named the state of being diverted.
items.cn: 名词 amusement 指被引开注意力的状态。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century, first for a pastime.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最初指消遣。

items.en: The meaning moved from idle musing toward laughter and entertainment.
items.cn: 词义从「闲看出神」转向「发笑与娱乐」。

items.en: Modern English uses it for feelings, pastimes, fairground rides and the leisure industry.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指感受、消遣、游乐设施与休闲产业。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the French verb muser is of uncertain origin, which is why no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；法语动词 muser 来源不确定，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: It is the base of the family.

items.exampleCN: 它把 muser 构成 amuser。

definition_zh: 轶事；趣闻；短小的纪实故事
definition_en: a short, usually amusing story about a real person or incident
core_image: 茶桌边有人讲起一件亲历的小事，听的人都笑了
scene: 饭桌上，老人讲起自己第一次进城时迷路的经历。She told an anecdote about her first day at work that made everyone laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 anecdote 是「轶事、趣闻」（第 1 个义项：关于真实人物或事件的短故事）；句意为她讲了一件上班第一天的趣事，把大家都逗笑了。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「轶事式的；传闻的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「根据轶事传闻地」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「爱讲轶事的人」

senses.title: A short story about something real
senses.titleCN: 关于真实事件的短故事
senses.definition: a brief account of a real incident or person, often entertaining
senses.definitionCN: 对真实事件或人物的简短叙述，常带有趣味
senses.example: She told an anecdote about her first day at work.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲了上班第一天的趣事。
senses.why: Greek anekdota meant 'things not published'; the word named private material later told aloud, and it kept the tone of a story shared rather than a formal record.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」；这个词原指后来被口头讲述的私人材料，因此保留了「分享故事」而非正式记录的语调。

senses.title: An unverified story
senses.definition: a story passed on without proof of its accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 没有证据证明其准确性便流传的说法
senses.example: The anecdote spread through the office before anyone checked it.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人核实，这件传闻就在办公室里传开了。
senses.why: Because such stories circulate by word of mouth, the word often carries a warning that the details may be unverified.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类故事靠口耳相传，这个词常带有「细节未必可靠」的提醒。

senses.title: An illustrative brief narrative
senses.definition: a short narrative used to make a point clearer
senses.definitionCN: 用来把论点讲得更清楚的短叙事
senses.example: He opened the lecture with an anecdote about Newton.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一则牛顿的轶事开场。
senses.why: Speakers borrow a small true story to carry a large idea, so the anecdote becomes a tool of explanation.
senses.whyCN: 演讲者借一个小而真实的故事承载大观念，于是轶事成了说明工具。

senses.title: Collected stories
senses.definition: a collection of such stories, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 这类故事的集合，常用复数形式
senses.example: The book is full of anecdotes about village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书里满是乡村生活的趣闻。
senses.why: Once many small stories are gathered, the plural names the whole collection rather than one telling.
senses.whyCN: 当许多小故事被收集起来，复数形式就指整部合集，而不是单次讲述。

intro.en: Anecdote goes back to a Greek word for things not published, a title given to a collection of private stories.
intro.cn: anecdote 可追溯到希腊语中表示「未发表之物」的词，那是一本私人故事集的标题。

items.en: The Greek prefix an- means 'not', the negative counterpart of a-.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 an- 意为「不」，是 a- 的否定形式。

items.en: ekdidonai meant 'to give out, publish', built from ek- 'out' and didonai 'to give'.
items.cn: ekdidonai 意为「交出、发表」，由 ek-（向外）与 didonai（给）构成。

items.en: ta anekdota meant 'things not published'; it was used as a title for private memoirs.
items.cn: ta anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」，曾被用作私人回忆录的标题。

items.en: French anecdote entered learned use in the seventeenth century with the sense of a short unpublished story.
items.cn: 法语 anecdote 在十七世纪进入学术用法，指未公开的短故事。

items.en: English adopted the word for a short story about a real person, often told for interest.
items.cn: 英语吸收该词，指关于真实人物的短故事，常为趣味而讲。

items.en: Modern usage extends anecdote to unverified gossip and to stories used as examples in speeches.
items.cn: 现代用法把 anecdote 扩展到未经证实的传闻，以及演讲中用作例子的故事。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, adverb, and person noun from the same family; the second gathers words for short narratives.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的形容词、副词与人物名词；第二组收表示短篇叙事的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning based on personal stories rather than proof.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「轶事式的、传闻的」，基于个人故事而非证据。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'by way of anecdote or unverified report'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「根据轶事传闻地」。

entries.definition: A person who collects or tells anecdotes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱讲轶事的人、轶事收集者」。

entries.definition: A general word for an account of events, real or invented.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「故事」，泛指对真实或虚构事件的叙述。

entries.definition: A narrative, often old or fictional and told aloud.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「故事、传说」，常指古老或虚构的口头叙事。

entries.definition: A factual description of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、描述」，对事件的事实性说明。

entries.definition: A long, often exaggerated story told informally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，非正式用法，义为「长篇故事」，常带夸张。

entries.definition: A single event or short period in a longer history.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插曲、片段」，较长历史中的单个事件或短时期。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Greek 'not published' origin and the common telling collocations; the abstract hooks picture the story being shared.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用希腊语「未发表」的来源与常见讲述搭配；抽象记忆点想象故事被分享的场景。

normal.en: Anecdote began as Greek 'things not published', so it still feels like a story let out of private life.
normal.cn: anecdote 原指希腊语「未发表之物」，因此仍像从私人生活中放出来的故事。

normal.en: Tell an anecdote and a personal anecdote are the standard patterns.
normal.cn: tell an anecdote 与 a personal anecdote 是标准结构。

normal.en: Anecdotal evidence is the adjective phrase for proof based on stories.
normal.cn: anecdotal evidence 是用故事作证据的形容词短语。

normal.en: The plural anecdotes often names a collection of such stories.
normal.cn: 复数 anecdotes 常指这类故事的合集。

normal.en: An anecdote differs from a joke: it claims to be true and usually has a point.
normal.cn: anecdote 与笑话不同：它声称真实，且通常有寓意。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of people around a table, one voice telling a small true story.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈人围坐桌边，一个声音讲着一件真实的小事。

abstract.en: Picture a folded note marked 'not published', later read aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着「未发表」的折纸，后来被当众读出。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker opening a lecture with one short story before the slides.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者在放幻灯片前先讲一个小故事。

examples.en: He told a funny anecdote about his first flight.
examples.cn: 他讲了一件第一次坐飞机的趣事。

examples.en: The article begins with an anecdote about a village teacher.
examples.cn: 文章以一则乡村教师的轶事开头。

examples.en: Her anecdotes made the long journey seem short.
examples.cn: 她的趣闻让漫长的旅程显得很短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安尼克多特」——一桌人围坐，有人翻出一件没发表过的小事来讲，就是轶事。

root: 希腊语 an-（不）+ ekdidonai（发表），名词 anekdota（未发表之物）；核心义是「原本私藏、后来讲出来的真实小故事」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a real short story, to unverified talk, to a story used as an example, to a whole collection of such stories.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从真实的短故事，走到未经证实的传闻，再走到用作例证的故事，最后是整部故事集。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small true story told around a table
core.cn: 核心意象：围坐桌边讲出的一件真实小事

branches.en: A real incident becomes a short spoken story.
branches.cn: 真实事件变成简短的讲述故事。

branches.en: Word of mouth turns the story into unverified gossip.
branches.cn: 口耳相传把故事变成未经证实的传闻。

branches.en: A speaker uses the story to make an idea concrete.
branches.cn: 演讲者用故事把观念讲得具体。

branches.en: Many stories together form a collection.
branches.cn: 许多故事合在一起成为合集。

branches.en: The same story can entertain and explain at once.
branches.cn: 同一个故事可以同时娱乐与说明。

intro.en: The word is built from Greek negative and publishing pieces, with the adjective, adverb, and person endings -al, -ly, and -ist.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的否定成分与「发表」成分构成，并带形容词、副词与人物后缀 -al、-ly、-ist。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the word is Greek in origin, and the Latin entries are left empty rather than inventing a form.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语祖先；这个词源自希腊语，因此拉丁条目留空，而不编造形式。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「轶事式的；传闻的」
名词，义为「爱讲轶事的人」

definition_en: the details of where someone lives, a formal speech, or to deal with a problem
core_image: 信封正面写着一行清楚的住址
scene: 会议上，主持人先请校长致辞，随后大家讨论如何解决停车难的问题。The mayor addressed the crowd from the steps.
sceneCN: 这里 address 是「向……讲话、致辞」（第 2 个义项：发表正式讲话）；句意为市长在台阶上向人群讲话。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ee 构成，义为「收件人」
过去分词作形容词，义为「写有地址的」
动名词，义为「称呼；处理」

senses.title: Where someone lives
senses.definition: the details of a place where a person or organization can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 可以联系到某人或某机构的地点信息
senses.example: Please write your home address on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上写下家庭住址。
senses.why: Old French adresser meant 'to straighten, to direct', and an address directs a letter to a place.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 adresser 意为「弄直、指向」，地址就是把信指向某个地方。

senses.title: A formal speech
senses.definition: a formal talk given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话
senses.example: The mayor addressed the crowd from the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 市长在台阶上向人群讲话。
senses.why: To address a group is to direct words at them, the same image as directing a letter.
senses.whyCN: 向一群人 address 就是把话指向他们，与把信指向某处是同一意象。

senses.title: To deal with a problem
senses.definition: to begin to deal with a problem or issue
senses.definitionCN: 着手处理问题或议题
senses.example: The council must address the housing shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 议会必须处理住房短缺问题。
senses.why: Modern usage turns the 'directing' image toward problems: attention is aimed at them until they are handled.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把「指向」意象转向问题：注意力对准问题直到解决。

intro.en: Address comes from Old French adresser, 'to straighten, to direct', from Latin ad- 'to' and directiare, 'to direct'.
intro.cn: address 来自古法语 adresser（弄直、指向），由拉丁语 ad-（向）与 directiare（引导）构成。

items.en: directus meant 'straight, direct'.
items.cn: directus 意为「直的、直接的」。

items.en: directiare meant 'to direct, to guide'.
items.cn: directiare 意为「引导、指向」。

items.en: adresser meant 'to straighten, to send toward'.
items.cn: adresser 意为「弄直、送往」。

items.en: English address first meant 'to direct or prepare'.
items.cn: 英语 address 最初意为「指向、准备」。

items.en: modern usage adds address a problem and email address.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了处理问题与电子邮箱地址。

note.en: The first group gathers the recipient and participle forms; the second gathers words for location, speech, and handling.
note.cn: 第一组收收件人与分词形式；第二组收表示地点、讲话与处理的词。

entries.definition: The person to whom a letter is sent.
The participle meaning 'written with an address'.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，义为「写有地址的」

entries.definition: The gerund meaning 'speaking to or handling'.
The place where something is.
A formal talk to an audience.
To deal with a problem energetically.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'direct' root and the envelope scene; the abstract hooks picture words aimed at a crowd or a problem.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「指向」词根与信封场景；抽象记忆点想象把话对准人群或问题。

normal.en: Address is 'to direct': a letter or words are aimed at a target.
normal.cn: address 是「指向」：信或话被对准目标。

normal.en: Home address and email address are the two fixed pairs.
normal.cn: home address 与 email address 是两个固定搭配。

normal.en: Deliver an address means give a speech.
normal.cn: deliver an address 指发表演讲。

normal.en: Address a problem means deal with it.
normal.cn: address a problem 指处理问题。

normal.en: The recipient is the addressee.
normal.cn: 收件人是 addressee。

abstract.en: Picture a clean line of writing on an envelope.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上一行清楚的住址。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker at a lectern facing a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者在讲台前面对人群。

abstract.en: Picture a committee turning to a housing list.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会转向住房清单。

examples.en: Please write your home address on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上写下家庭住址。

examples.en: The mayor addressed the crowd from the steps.
examples.cn: 市长在台阶上向人群讲话。

examples.en: The council must address the housing shortage.
examples.cn: 议会必须处理住房短缺问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德雷斯」——把话或信对准某个地方，就是地址或致辞。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ directiare（引导）→ 法语 adresser（指向）；核心义是「把某物指向一个目标」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a place to reach someone, to a speech aimed at a crowd, to attention aimed at a problem.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从联系某人的地点，走到对准人群的讲话，再到对准问题的注意力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words or a letter aimed at a target
core.cn: 核心意象：话或信被对准目标

branches.en: The details of where someone can be reached.
branches.cn: 联系某人的地点信息。

branches.en: A formal speech to an audience.
branches.cn: 面向听众的正式讲话。

branches.en: To deal with a problem.
branches.cn: 处理问题。

branches.en: A letter and a speech are both aimed.
branches.cn: 信与演讲都是被指向的。

branches.en: Words and attention are both directed at a target.
branches.cn: 言语与注意力都对准目标。

intro.en: The word joins the prefix ad- (to) with the direct root dress-, and its family adds recipient and participle forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把前缀 ad-（向）与「引导」词根 dress- 结合，词族另加收件人与分词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin directiare is the remote source, recorded here with directus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 directiare 是远源，这里连同 directus 一并记录。
