derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「收件人」
形容词，义为「写有地址的」

definition_zh: 角；角度；视角；角落；斜移；钓鱼
definition_en: the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, a point of view, or to turn or fish at a slant
core_image: 两条线在一点相交，张开一个口子
scene: 摄影师蹲下来，让镜头从低处仰拍那座桥。The photographer changed the angle to make the bridge look taller.
sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角度、视角」（第 1 个义项：观察或拍摄的方向）；句意为摄影师改变角度，让桥显得更高。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有角的；棱角分明的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「钓鱼者；角鱼」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「钓鱼（活动）」

senses.title: A geometric angle
senses.definition: the figure formed by two lines meeting at a point, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线在一点相交形成的图形，以度数计量
senses.example: The two walls meet at a right angle.
senses.exampleCN: 两面墙以直角相交。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant 'corner'; a corner is where two edges meet, and the opening between them became the measurable angle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、角落」；角落是两条边相交之处，它们之间张开的口子就成了可测量的角。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of considering a situation
senses.definitionCN: 考虑某种情况的特定方式
senses.example: Try to see the problem from a different angle.
senses.exampleCN: 试着从不同角度看这个问题。
senses.why: Thinking is imagined as looking: the place from which one looks determines what one sees, so angle becomes viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 思考被想象成观看：观看的位置决定所见，于是 angle 变成视角。

senses.title: A corner or slanting position
senses.definition: a corner of a room or an object placed at a slant
senses.definitionCN: 房间的角落，或以倾斜方式放置的位置
senses.example: The chair stood at an angle to the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子斜对着墙放着。
senses.why: The physical corner sense survives in descriptions of objects that meet or lean at an opening.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的「角落」义保留在描述物体相交或倾斜放置的说法中。

senses.title: To slant or turn
senses.definition: to move or place something at a slant
senses.definitionCN: 使某物倾斜移动或放置
senses.example: She angled the mirror toward the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她把镜子斜向窗户。
senses.why: The verb turns the corner into an action: an object is given an angle rather than standing square.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「角」变成动作：物体被摆成一个角度，而不是方方正正地立着。

senses.title: To fish, or to seek indirectly
senses.definition: to fish with a hook, or to try to get something indirectly
senses.definitionCN: 用鱼钩钓鱼，或间接地谋求某物
senses.example: He angled for an invitation to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他拐弯抹角地想弄到一张晚宴请柬。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word for a fishhook; the shared spelling hides two separate histories.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个表示「鱼钩」的古英语词；相同的拼写掩盖了两段不同的历史。

intro.en: Angle the corner word comes from Latin, while angle the fishing word comes from Old English; the two met in spelling, not in origin.
intro.cn: 表示「角」的 angle 来自拉丁语，表示「钓鱼」的 angle 来自古英语；二者是在拼写上相遇，而非同源。

items.en: angulus meant 'a corner', and it produced triangle and angular.
items.cn: angulus 意为「角、角落」，衍生出 triangle 与 angular。

items.en: Old French angle carried the geometric sense into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 angle 把几何义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: English angle is recorded from the fourteenth century for a corner or a meeting of lines.
items.cn: 英语 angle 自十四世纪有记录，指角落或线条相交。

items.en: A separate Old English word angul meant 'fishhook'; its verb anglian gave the fishing sense.
items.cn: 另一个古英语词 angul 意为「鱼钩」；其动词 anglian 产生了钓鱼义。

items.en: The two words fell together in spelling, and the geometric word later developed the figurative 'point of view'.
items.cn: 两个词在拼写上合并，几何词后来发展出比喻性的「观点」义。

items.en: The verb now covers slanting objects as well as fishing and indirect seeking.
items.cn: 动词如今既覆盖使物体倾斜，也覆盖钓鱼与间接谋求。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and the two fishing forms; the second gathers words for viewpoint and slant.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与两个钓鱼形式；第二组收表示视角与倾斜的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning having angles or sharp corners.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有角的、棱角分明的」。

entries.definition: A person who fishes with a hook; it belongs to the Old English fishhook word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钓鱼者」，属于古英语「鱼钩」那一支。

entries.definition: The activity of fishing with a rod and line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钓鱼活动」，用竿线垂钓。

entries.definition: A three-sided shape, literally a figure with three corners.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「三角形」，字面是「三个角的图形」。

entries.definition: A person's way of looking at a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观点、视角」，一个人看问题的方式。

entries.definition: A particular way of seeing things, often shaped by experience.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视角、看法」，常由经历塑造的观察方式。

entries.definition: A sloping direction or a biased way of presenting something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倾斜」或「倾向性看法」。

entries.definition: The point where two edges or walls meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「角落」，两条边或墙相交之处。

entries.definition: A sloping position or the act of sloping.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「倾斜」或「使倾斜」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin corner and the common 'from a different angle'; the abstract hooks picture the opening between two lines.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「角落」与常见结构 from a different angle；抽象记忆点想象两条线之间张开的口子。

normal.en: Angle and triangle share Latin angulus, 'corner'.
normal.cn: angle 与 triangle 共享拉丁语 angulus（角）。

normal.en: A right angle is ninety degrees; an acute angle is smaller.
normal.cn: right angle 是九十度；acute angle 更小。

normal.en: From a different angle is the standard phrase for another viewpoint.
normal.cn: from a different angle 是表示「换个视角」的标准短语。

normal.en: The fishing sense comes from Old English angul, a fishhook, not from Latin.
normal.cn: 钓鱼义来自古英语 angul（鱼钩），而非拉丁语。

normal.en: Camera angle describes where the lens is placed.
normal.cn: camera angle 描述镜头放置的位置。

abstract.en: Picture two lines meeting at a point and opening like a pair of scissors.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线在一点相交，像剪刀一样张开。

abstract.en: Picture a photographer lying on the ground to shoot upward.
abstract.cn: 想象摄影师趴在地上向上拍摄。

abstract.en: Picture a chair leaning against a wall instead of facing it squarely.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子斜靠墙边，而不是正对墙面。

examples.en: The roof rises at a steep angle.
examples.cn: 屋顶以很陡的角度升起。

examples.en: We should consider the plan from a new angle.
examples.cn: 我们应该从新的角度考虑这个计划。

examples.en: He angled the lamp toward the book.
examples.cn: 他把灯斜向书本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安格尔」——两条线在角上相交，张开的那个口子就是角度。

root: 拉丁语 angulus（角、角落），经古法语 angle 进入英语；钓鱼义另来自古英语 angul（鱼钩），二者同形不同源

sensesIntro.en: The senses cover the geometric corner, the viewpoint taken from a position, a slanting placement, the act of slanting, and the separate fishing word.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项覆盖几何角、由位置决定的视角、倾斜的摆放、使倾斜的动作，以及另一个同形的钓鱼词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines meeting and opening at a point
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线在一点相交并张开

branches.en: The measurable opening between two meeting lines.
branches.cn: 两条相交线之间可测量的开口。

branches.en: Where one stands determines what one sees, so angle becomes viewpoint.
branches.cn: 人所站的位置决定所见，于是 angle 成为视角。

branches.en: Physical corners and slanted placements, as noun and verb.
branches.cn: 物理角落与倾斜摆放，兼作名词与动词。

branches.en: A separate Old English fishhook word gives the fishing sense.
branches.cn: 另一个古英语鱼钩词给出钓鱼义。

branches.en: A corner can also be the place from which a view is taken.
branches.cn: 角落也可以是取景的立足点。

intro.en: The geometric family is built from the Latin stem angul-, with adjective, agent, and activity endings; the fishing family comes from the Old English hook word.
intro.cn: 几何词族由拉丁词干 angul- 加形容词、施动者与活动后缀构成；钓鱼词族来自古英语鱼钩词。

latinIntro.en: Latin angulus is the direct source of the geometric word, so the Latin entries record the noun and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angulus 是几何词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录名词与派生形容词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「有角的；棱角分明的」
名词，义为「钓鱼者；角鱼」

definition_en: enough in amount, or good enough in quality for a particular purpose
core_image: 水位刚好到刻度线，不多也不少
scene: 检查员量了量水箱，确认存量还能撑到下一次补给。The supply is adequate for the whole winter.
sceneCN: 这里 adequate 是「足够的」（第 1 个义项：数量上够用）；句意为储备足够整个冬天使用。

derivatives.zh: 加 -acy 构成，义为「足够；适当」
加 -ly 构成，义为「充分地」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不足的」

senses.title: Enough in amount
senses.definition: enough for a particular need or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 满足特定需要或用途的数量
senses.example: The supply is adequate for the whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 储备足够整个冬天使用。
senses.why: Latin adaequatus meant 'made equal to', so adequate describes a quantity that matches the demand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adaequatus 意为「与……相等」，因此 adequate 描述与需求相称的数量。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: of a standard that is acceptable, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 达到可接受标准，但并非优秀
senses.example: The room was adequate but not comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 这房间还算够用，但不算舒适。
senses.why: The same 'equal to the task' image applies to quality: something adequate meets the bar without exceeding it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「与任务相称」意象也用于质量：adequate 达标而不超额。

intro.en: Adequate comes from Latin adaequatus, 'made equal to', from ad- 'to' and aequare, 'to make equal'.
intro.cn: adequate 来自拉丁语 adaequatus（使相等），由 ad-（向）与 aequare（使相等）构成。

items.en: aequus meant 'equal, level', the root of equal.
items.cn: aequus 意为「相等的、平的」，是 equal 的词根。

items.en: aequare meant 'to make equal, to level'.
items.cn: aequare 意为「使相等、弄平」。

items.en: adaequatus meant 'made equal to'.
items.cn: adaequatus 意为「与……相等的」。

items.en: English adequate first meant 'equal to a requirement'.
items.cn: 英语 adequate 最初意为「与要求相称」。

items.en: modern usage adds adequate supply and adequate evidence.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了充足供应与充分证据。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and negative family; the second gathers adjectives of sufficiency.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与否定词族；第二组收表示充足的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for sufficiency.
The adverb meaning 'well enough'.
The negative adjective for 'not enough'.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形容词，义为「不足的」

entries.definition: Enough for a need, often in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的」，较正式。

entries.definition: Good enough to be accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的」

entries.definition: Of a standard that can be allowed.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'made equal' root and the water gauge; the abstract hooks picture a level exactly at the mark.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「使相等」词根与水尺；抽象记忆点想象水位正好到刻度线。

normal.en: Adequate is 'equal to the need': aequus means equal.
normal.cn: adequate 是「与需求相等」：aequus 意为相等。

normal.en: Adequate for is the key pattern.
normal.cn: adequate for 是关键搭配。

normal.en: Barely adequate means only just enough.
normal.cn: barely adequate 指勉强够用。

normal.en: The noun is adequacy, the negative inadequate.
normal.cn: 名词是 adequacy，否定形式是 inadequate。

normal.en: Sufficient is more formal; adequate is neutral.
normal.cn: sufficient 更正式，adequate 中性。

abstract.en: Picture water sitting exactly at the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象水位正好停在刻度线。

abstract.en: Picture a meal that fills but does not delight.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿吃饱但不惊喜的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a room that meets the standard, no more.
abstract.cn: 想象房间刚达标，没有多余。

examples.en: The supply is adequate for the whole winter.
examples.cn: 储备足够整个冬天使用。

examples.en: The room was adequate but not comfortable.
examples.cn: 这房间还算够用，但不算舒适。

examples.en: We have adequate evidence to support the claim.
examples.cn: 我们有充分证据支持这一说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪夸特」——正好与需求齐平，就是足够。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ aequare（使相等）→ adaequatus；核心义是「与需求相称、刚好够」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from enough in amount, to acceptable in quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从数量足够，走到质量合格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water exactly at the mark
core.cn: 核心意象：水位正好停在刻度线

branches.en: Enough for a particular need.
branches.cn: 满足特定需要的数量。

branches.en: Good enough in quality.
branches.cn: 质量上达到可接受标准。

branches.en: Quantity and quality are both matched to a task.
branches.cn: 数量与质量都与任务相称。

branches.en: Adequate stops at the bar; excellent goes beyond.
branches.cn: adequate 停在线内，excellent 才越线。

branches.en: The negative inadequate covers both senses.
branches.cn: 否定形式 inadequate 涵盖两个义项。

intro.en: The adjective joins the prefix ad- (to) with the equal root equ- and the participle ending -ate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把前缀 ad-（向）与「相等」词根 equ- 及分词后缀 -ate 结合。

latinIntro.en: Latin adaequatus is the direct ancestor, recorded here with aequare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adaequatus 是直接祖先，这里连同 aequare 一并记录。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「足够」
形容词，义为「不足的」

definition_zh: 有生命的；活的；使有生气；把……做成动画；驱动
definition_en: living, or having the quality of life; also to give life, energy, or motion to something
core_image: 一口气吹进泥人，泥人的胸口开始起伏
scene: 动画师让画里的小人抬起手，一帧一帧地动起来。The animator made the drawn figure raise its hand and animate frame by frame.
sceneCN: 这里 animate 是「使动起来、做成动画」（第 5 个义项：逐帧赋予画面运动）；句意为动画师让画中的小人抬手，一帧一帧地活动起来。

pos.zh: 形容词：有生命的；活的；活泼的
动词：使有生气；驱动；制作动画

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「动画；生气；活力」
由动词加施动者后缀构成，义为「动画师；赋予生气者」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「动画的；生气勃勃的」
由拉丁词根加名词后缀构成，义为「有生性」，语言学指名词的生命度

senses.title: Having life
senses.definition: possessing life, as opposed to lifeless matter
senses.definitionCN: 具有生命，与无生命的物质相对
senses.example: Plants and animals are animate beings.
senses.exampleCN: 植物与动物都是有生命的存在物。
senses.why: Latin anima meant breath or soul, and whatever has it is alive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anima 意为「气息、灵魂」，拥有它的东西就是活的。

senses.title: Lively in manner
senses.definition: full of energy and spirit in behaviour or expression
senses.definitionCN: 行为或表达中充满精力与精神
senses.example: Her animate gestures held the audience's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 她生动的动作吸引了观众的注意。
senses.why: The quality of having a soul shows outward as liveliness.
senses.whyCN: 「有灵魂」的特质在外表上就表现为活泼。

senses.title: To enliven someone or something
senses.definition: to fill a person, group, or event with energy and interest
senses.definitionCN: 使人、群体或活动充满精力与兴趣
senses.example: The moderator animated the quiet panel with a direct question.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人用一个直接的问题让沉闷的座谈活跃起来。
senses.why: To animate is to put breath into a room that had gone flat.
senses.whyCN: animate 就是给沉闷的场合吹进一口气。

senses.title: To drive a mechanism
senses.definition: to supply motion or power to a device or system
senses.definitionCN: 为装置或系统提供运动或动力
senses.example: A small motor animates the model's rotating platform.
senses.exampleCN: 一台小马达驱动模型的可旋转平台。
senses.why: Motion is the visible sign of life, so machines that move are said to be animated.
senses.whyCN: 运动是生命最可见的标志，因此会动的机械被说成被赋予了生命。

senses.title: To make an animation
senses.definition: to create the illusion of movement by filming or drawing successive frames
senses.definitionCN: 通过拍摄或绘制连续画面制造运动错觉
senses.example: The animator made the drawn figure raise its hand and animate frame by frame.
senses.exampleCN: 动画师让画中的小人抬手，一帧一帧地活动起来。
senses.why: Film repeats the old dream of giving pictures life.
senses.whyCN: 电影重复了古老的梦想：让图画活起来。

senses.title: To give spirit to art
senses.definition: to fill a painting, story, or performance with expressive life
senses.definitionCN: 使绘画、故事或表演充满表现力与生命感
senses.example: The sculptor animated the stone with a twisting pose.
senses.exampleCN: 雕塑家用一个扭身的姿态让石头有了生气。
senses.why: Artists speak of animating material the way the soul animates the body.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家说「赋予材料生命」，正如灵魂赋予身体生命。

senses.title: Grammatically animate
senses.definition: belonging to the grammatical class of living things, which affects case and agreement in some languages
senses.definitionCN: 属于语法上的「生命」类别，在有些语言中影响格与一致关系
senses.example: In that language, animate nouns take a different ending.
senses.exampleCN: 在那门语言里，有生名词使用不同的词尾。
senses.why: Grammar inherited the old distinction between living and non-living things.
senses.whyCN: 语法继承了古老的「生物与非生物」之分。

senses.title: Animate nature
senses.definition: in the phrase animate nature, the whole world of animals as distinct from plants and minerals
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 animate nature，指与植物、矿物相区别的整个动物界
senses.example: The exhibition divided animate nature from the mineral kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把动物界与矿物界分开陈列。
senses.why: Animate serves as the adjective of the animal kingdom in older scientific writing.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的科学写作中，animate 充当「动物界」的形容词。

intro.en: Animate descends from a Latin word for breath, the same root that gives animal and animosity.
intro.cn: animate 源自拉丁语表示「气息」的词，animal 与 animosity 也出自同一词根。

items.en: anima meant 'breath, air, soul, life'.
items.cn: anima 意为「气息、空气、灵魂、生命」。

items.en: animare meant 'to give life to, quicken, inspire'.
items.cn: animare 意为「赋予生命、使活跃、鼓舞」。

items.en: The participle animatus meant 'living, having been given life'.
items.cn: 分词 animatus 意为「有生命的、被赋予生命的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective first, then the verb, in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语先借入形容词，十六世纪前后又借入动词。

items.en: The rise of animation gave animate a new commercial sense: to make drawings and models move on screen.
items.cn: 动画产业的兴起给 animate 添了新的商业义：让图画与模型在屏幕上动起来。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from biology and grammar to motors, sculpture and animation studios.
items.cn: 现代用法从生物学、语法延伸到马达、雕塑与动画工作室。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the breath-root family and its negative; the near-meaning group gathers words for life and liveliness.
note.cn: 形近组收「气息」词根词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示生命与活泼的词。

entries.definition: The technique of making drawings or models appear to move, or the quality of being lively.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动画；生气」，让图画或模型看似会动的技术，也指活泼。

entries.definition: A person who makes animations.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动画师」，制作动画的人。

entries.definition: Full of energy, or made into an animation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「生气勃勃的；动画的」。

entries.definition: Not alive; the prefix in- reverses the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无生命的」，前缀 in- 反转了形容词含义。

entries.definition: Alive; currently having life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活着的」，当前具有生命。

entries.definition: Living, not dead.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活着的」，未死亡的。

entries.definition: Full of energy and quick movement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「活泼的；有活力的」。

entries.definition: To make something more interesting or cheerful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使活跃；使有趣」。

entries.definition: To give life or strength to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使有生气；赋予生命」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the breath root, the clay-figure image, and the move from biology to film.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用「气息」词根、泥人的意象，以及从生物学到电影的延伸。

normal.en: anima is breath or soul; to animate is to put breath into something.
normal.cn: anima 是气息或灵魂；animate 就是往某物里吹气。

normal.en: The adjective means alive; the verb means to make alive or to make move.
normal.cn: 形容词义为「活的」，动词义为「使有生命」或「使动起来」。

normal.en: Animate nature is the animal kingdom in older science writing.
normal.cn: animate nature 是较早科学写作中的「动物界」。

normal.en: Animated cartoons are literally drawings given motion.
normal.cn: 动画片字面上就是被赋予运动的图画。

normal.en: The negative is inanimate, meaning without life.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 inanimate，意为「无生命的」。

abstract.en: Picture breath entering a clay figure until its chest rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一口气吹进泥人，直到它的胸口起伏。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of drawings flipped so a figure walks.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠画被快速翻动，画中人走了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a small motor turning a model platform.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小马达带动模型平台旋转。

examples.en: Plants and animals are animate beings.
examples.cn: 植物与动物都是有生命的存在物。

examples.en: The animator made the drawn figure raise its hand and animate frame by frame.
examples.cn: 动画师让画中的小人抬手，一帧一帧地活动起来。

examples.en: The moderator animated the quiet panel with a direct question.
examples.cn: 主持人用一个直接的问题让沉闷的座谈活跃起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安尼美特」——安尼吹一口气进泥人，泥人胸口一起一伏，画稿也跟着动起来

root: 拉丁语 anima「气息、灵魂」→ animare「赋予生命、使活跃」→ animatus → 英语 animate；形容词义「有生命的」，动词义「使有生气、驱动、制作动画」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of animate move from living beings through liveliness, enlivening, motors, animation, art, grammatical animacy and the animal kingdom.
sensesIntro.cn: animate 的八个义项从有生命的存在物，延伸到活泼、鼓舞、驱动、动画、艺术、语法有生性与动物界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath enters a clay figure and its chest rises.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气吹进泥人，胸口起伏。

branches.en: THE LIVING: having life shows outwardly as liveliness.
branches.cn: 生命线：拥有生命，在外表上表现为活泼。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: rooms, art and stone can all be given energy.
branches.cn: 精神线：房间、艺术与石头都能被注入活力。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: motors give motion to what cannot live.
branches.cn: 机械线：马达给不能活的东西以运动。

branches.en: THE FRAME: film gives drawings the illusion of life.
branches.cn: 帧线：电影给图画以生命的错觉。

branches.en: THE CLASS: grammar and older biology sort the living from the non-living.
branches.cn: 分类线：语法与早期生物学区分生物与非生物。

intro.en: Animate is built from a Latin breath root plus a verb and participial ending; English added the agent and noun endings.
intro.cn: animate 由拉丁语「气息」词根加动词与分词词尾构成；英语又加了施动者与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The family is attested: anima, animare and animatus all appear in Latin texts.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族有文献可证：anima、animare 与 animatus 均见于拉丁文本。

definition_zh: 每年的；年度的；一年一度的；年刊；一年生植物
definition_en: happening once every year, measured over a year, or a yearly publication or plant
core_image: 日历翻过十二页，回到同一个标记日期
scene: 公司每年三月都办一次全员大会，员工提前一周就知道日期。The company holds its annual meeting in March.
sceneCN: 这里 annual 是「每年的、一年一度的」（第 1 个义项：每年发生一次）；句意为公司每年三月举行年度会议。

pos.zh: 每年的；一年一度的；按年计算的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「每年地、按年地」
由动词 annualize 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「按年折算的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「按年折算」

senses.title: Happening once every year
senses.definition: taking place once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生一次的
senses.example: The annual meeting is held every March.
senses.exampleCN: 年度会议每年三月举行。
senses.why: Latin annus 'year' gave annuus 'yearly'; the adjective marks an event that returns on the same point of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annus（年）派生出 annuus（每年的）；这个形容词标记在日历同一点上回归的事件。

senses.title: Measured or calculated over a year
senses.definition: counted or averaged across a full year
senses.definitionCN: 按整年统计或平均的
senses.example: The annual rainfall in this valley is about eight hundred millimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的年降雨量约为八百毫米。
senses.why: The same year-word also labels any quantity summed over twelve months, so figures and totals take the adjective too.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「年」词也标记任何按十二个月加总的数量，因此数字与总额也用这个形容词。

senses.title: A publication issued once a year
senses.definition: a book or magazine published once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版一次的书籍或刊物
senses.example: The school annual lists every graduate of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 学校年刊登出了那一年的全部毕业生。
senses.why: When a publication appears on a yearly rhythm, the adjective turns into a noun naming the book itself.
senses.whyCN: 当出版物按年发行，形容词就转为名词，直接指这本书。

senses.title: A plant that lives for one year
senses.definition: a plant that completes its life cycle within a single growing season
senses.definitionCN: 在一个生长季内完成生命周期的植物
senses.example: Marigolds are grown as annuals in cold regions.
senses.exampleCN: 在寒冷地区，万寿菊作为一年生植物栽培。
senses.why: Gardening borrows the year-word for plants whose whole life fits inside one season, as opposed to perennials.
senses.whyCN: 园艺借用这个「年」词，指整个生命只占一个生长季的植物，与多年生植物相对。

intro.en: Annual comes from the Latin word for year, through the adjective annuus and the later annualis.
intro.cn: annual 来自拉丁语中表示「年」的词，经形容词 annuus 与后来的 annualis 演变而来。

items.en: annus meant 'year', and it also gave annals and anniversary.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，也衍生出 annals 与 anniversary。

items.en: The adjective annuus meant 'yearly, lasting a year'.
items.cn: 形容词 annuus 意为「每年的、持续一年的」。

items.en: Later Latin annualis carried the yearly sense into learned and church use.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 annualis 把「每年」义带入学术与教会用语。

items.en: Old French annuel passed the adjective to English with the same yearly meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 annuel 把同一「每年」义传给英语。

items.en: English annual first named a mass said yearly, then any yearly event or account.
items.cn: 英语 annual 最初指每年举行的弥撒，后来指任何年度事件或账目。

items.en: Modern usage adds the yearly publication and the one-season garden plant.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了年刊，以及只活一个生长季的园艺植物。

note.en: The first group gathers near-spellings that are often confused; the second gathers words that also express a yearly rhythm.
note.cn: 第一组收易混的近形词；第二组收同样表达「按年」节奏的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to cancel or declare invalid, from a Latin word for 'nothing'.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废除、宣告无效」，来自拉丁语「无」一词。

entries.definition: A yearly record of events, always plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「编年史」，恒用复数，按年记录事件。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid each year, especially to a retiree.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「年金」，每年支付的固定金额。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to heat and cool metal or glass to make it stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「退火」，加热后缓慢冷却以增强金属或玻璃。

entries.definition: An adjective or adverb meaning once a year.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「每年的、每年一次」。

entries.definition: A Latin phrase used in finance for 'each year'.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁短语，金融用语，义为「每年」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening every two years.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「两年一次的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something that happens again, without saying how often.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反复出现的」，不限定间隔。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin year-word and the common yearly collocations; the abstract hooks picture a calendar returning to the same date.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「年」词根与常见年度搭配；抽象记忆点想象日历翻回同一个日期。

normal.en: Annual shares Latin annus with anniversary and annals.
normal.cn: annual 与 anniversary、annals 共享拉丁语 annus（年）。

normal.en: Annual report and annual meeting are the two most common business phrases.
normal.cn: annual report 与 annual meeting 是商务中最常见的两个短语。

normal.en: Annually is the adverb, and it regularly follows figures.
normal.cn: annually 是副词，常跟在数字之后。

normal.en: A plant called an annual finishes its life in one season.
normal.cn: 被称为 annual 的植物在一个生长季内结束生命。

normal.en: Do not confuse annual with annul, which means to cancel.
normal.cn: 不要把 annual 与 annul 混淆，后者意为废除。

abstract.en: Picture a wall calendar peeling back to one circled date.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上日历一页页撕回同一个圈出的日期。

abstract.en: Picture a thick yearbook handed out once each spring.
abstract.cn: 想象每年春天发一次的那本厚年鉴。

abstract.en: Picture a marigold sprouting, flowering, and dying before autumn.
abstract.cn: 想象一株万寿菊在秋天前发芽、开花、枯萎。

examples.en: The firm publishes its annual report every March.
examples.cn: 公司每年三月发布年度报告。

examples.en: Her annual income grew after the promotion.
examples.cn: 升职后她的年收入增加了。

examples.en: Some farmers treat these flowers as annuals.
examples.cn: 有些农户把这些花当作一年生植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安纽尔」——日历翻过十二个月，回到同一个标记日，就是每年的。

root: 拉丁语 annus（年）→ annuus（每年的）→ annualis；核心义是「在一年节点上回归或按整年统计」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the yearly event, to a yearly total, to the yearly publication, to the plant that lives one season.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从每年发生的事件，走到按年统计的总额，再到每年出版的刊物，最后是只活一季的植物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar returning to the same marked date
core.cn: 核心意象：日历翻回同一个标记日期

branches.en: The event that returns once each year.
branches.cn: 每年返回一次的事件。

branches.en: Figures summed or averaged over the whole year.
branches.cn: 按整年加总或平均的数字。

branches.en: A book that appears on the yearly rhythm.
branches.cn: 按年节奏出版的书籍。

branches.en: A plant whose whole life fits in one growing season.
branches.cn: 整个生命只占一个生长季的植物。

branches.en: The yearly rhythm produces a yearly publication.
branches.cn: 按年的节奏产生了年度出版物。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin year stem ann-, with adjective, adverb, and verb endings.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁语「年」词干 ann- 加形容词、副词与动词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin annus and annuus are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record both the noun and the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 annus 与 annuus 是直接祖先，因此拉丁条目同时记录名词与形容词。

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「每年地；按年地」
名词，义为「按年折算」

definition_en: to stick to a surface, or to follow a rule, belief, or plan closely
core_image: 胶带紧紧贴住纸面，撕开时还带走一层纤维
scene: 标签贴上去以后再揭，纸面已经被粘掉一小块。All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里 adhere 是「遵守、坚持」（第 2 个义项：紧紧遵循规则或信念）；句意为全体员工必须遵守安全规定。

derivatives.zh: 加 -sion 构成，义为「粘附；附着力」
加 -ive 构成，义为「粘性的；粘合剂」
加 -ent 构成，义为「拥护者；附着的」

senses.title: Stick to a surface
senses.definition: to stick firmly to a surface
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢贴在某个表面上
senses.example: The label adhered to the glass even after washing.
senses.exampleCN: 洗过之后标签仍粘在玻璃上。
senses.why: Latin adhaerere meant 'to stick to', built on haerere, 'to stick', so the physical sense is the oldest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adhaerere 意为「粘住」，由 haerere（粘）构成，因此物理义最古老。

senses.title: Follow a rule or belief
senses.definition: to stay close to a rule, belief, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧遵循规则、信念或计划
senses.example: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工必须遵守安全规定。
senses.why: A person can also 'stick' to a principle, so the physical image becomes loyalty to a standard.
senses.whyCN: 人也能「粘」在一条原则上，因此物理意象变成对标准的忠诚。

intro.en: Adhere comes from Latin adhaerere, 'to stick to', from ad- 'to' and haerere, 'to stick or cling'.
intro.cn: adhere 来自拉丁语 adhaerere（粘住），由 ad-（向）与 haerere（粘、贴）构成。

items.en: haerere meant 'to stick, to cling'.
items.cn: haerere 意为「粘、贴」。

items.en: adhaerere meant 'to stick to'.
items.cn: adhaerere 意为「粘住」。

items.en: adhaesio named the state of sticking.
items.cn: adhaesio 指粘附状态。

items.en: English adhere first described physical sticking.
items.cn: 英语 adhere 最初描述物理粘附。

items.en: modern usage adds adhere to rules and beliefs.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了遵守规则与坚持信念。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and adjective family; the second gathers verbs of sticking and complying.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与形容词词族；第二组收表示粘附与遵守的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of sticking.
A substance that sticks things together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词/形容词，义为「粘合剂；粘性的」

entries.definition: A supporter who sticks to a cause.
To attach or remain attached.
To hold on tightly to something.
To follow a rule or order.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the stick root and the label scene; the abstract hooks picture a rule that a person stays glued to.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「粘」词根与标签场景；抽象记忆点想象人紧紧粘在一条规则上。

normal.en: Adhere is 'to stick to': haerere means stick.
normal.cn: adhere 是「粘住」：haerere 意为粘。

normal.en: Adhere to takes both surfaces and rules.
normal.cn: adhere to 既可接表面，也可接规则。

normal.en: Adhesive is the glue; adhesion is the grip.
normal.cn: adhesive 是胶，adhesion 是粘附力。

normal.en: Comply is the legal twin for the second sense.
normal.cn: comply 是第二义项的法律近亲。

normal.en: An adherent sticks to a cause, not a wall.
normal.cn: an adherent 粘的是事业，不是墙。

abstract.en: Picture a label lifting fibres from paper.
abstract.cn: 想象标签揭起时带下纸纤维。

abstract.en: Picture a poster staying on a wet wall.
abstract.cn: 想象海报贴在湿墙上不掉。

abstract.en: Picture a worker refusing to skip a safety step.
abstract.cn: 想象工人拒绝跳过安全步骤。

examples.en: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
examples.cn: 全体员工必须遵守安全规定。

examples.en: The label adhered to the glass even after washing.
examples.cn: 洗过之后标签仍粘在玻璃上。

examples.en: She adhered to her plan despite the criticism.
examples.cn: 尽管受到批评，她仍坚持自己的计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德希尔」——像胶一样贴住不放，就是粘附或坚持。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ haerere（粘）→ adhaerere；核心义是「紧紧贴住不放」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical sticking, to loyalty to a rule or belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理粘附，走到对规则或信念的坚守。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stuck so firmly it lifts paper
core.cn: 核心意象：标签粘得能带下纸纤维

branches.en: To stick firmly to a surface.
branches.cn: 牢牢贴在表面上。

branches.en: To follow a rule or belief closely.
branches.cn: 紧紧遵循规则或信念。

branches.en: Physical sticking becomes moral loyalty.
branches.cn: 物理粘附变成道德忠诚。

branches.en: Adhere to is the shared pattern.
branches.cn: adhere to 是共用搭配。

branches.en: Both senses mean not letting go.
branches.cn: 两个义项都表示不松手。

intro.en: The verb joins the prefix ad- (to) with the stick root her- and a short verb ending, and its family adds noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: 这个动词把前缀 ad-（向）与「粘」词根 her- 及短动词词尾结合，词族另加名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin adhaerere is the direct ancestor, recorded here with haerere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adhaerere 是直接祖先，这里连同 haerere 一并记录。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「粘附」
形容词/名词，义为「粘性的；粘合剂」

definition_zh: 触角；天线；敏锐的感知力
definition_en: a feeler on an insect's head, a device that sends or receives radio waves, or a natural sensitivity to signals
core_image: 头顶伸出的一对细长探杆，向四面试探
scene: 雨后墙角的蚂蚁排成纵队，前面的用头顶细须互相碰触传递方向。The ants touch antennae to follow the scent trail.
sceneCN: 这里 antenna 是「触角」（第 1 个义项：昆虫头部的感觉器官）；句意为蚂蚁用触角相碰来跟随气味路径。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「触角的」
由本词加指小后缀构成，义为「小触角」

senses.title: An insect's feeler
senses.definition: one of a pair of slender feelers on an insect's head, used for touch and smell
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫头部一对细长的感觉器，用于触觉与嗅觉
senses.example: The beetle waved its antennae to test the air.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫摆动触角试探空气。
senses.why: Latin antenna first meant the yard of a sail; its long projecting shape was borrowed by naturalists for the insect's feelers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antenna 原指帆船上的横桁；其细长外伸的形状被博物学家借用来指昆虫的触角。

senses.title: A radio or television aerial
senses.definition: a metal device that sends out or picks up radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 发送或接收无线电波的金属装置
senses.example: The old radio needs a longer antenna to pick up that station.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机需要更长的天线才能收到那个电台。
senses.why: Wireless engineers reused the same word for the projecting rods on a roof, because a mast-yard and an aerial share the long arm reaching into the air.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师把同一个词用给屋顶上外伸的金属杆，因为帆桁与天线都是伸向空中的长臂。

senses.title: A sensitivity to signals
senses.definition: a natural ability to notice signs or opportunities
senses.definitionCN: 察觉迹象或机会的天赋
senses.example: A good reporter has an antenna for a story others miss.
senses.exampleCN: 好记者对别人漏掉的新闻有敏锐的嗅觉。
senses.why: If feelers detect what is faintly there, the word can name a person's inner feeler for trends and moods.
senses.whyCN: 既然触角能察觉微弱存在，这个词便可指名一个人对趋势与情绪的内在触角。

intro.en: Antenna began as the name of a sail yard, was borrowed for insect feelers, and was borrowed again for wireless aerials.
intro.cn: antenna 最初指帆船横桁，先被借去指昆虫触角，又被借去指无线电天线。

items.en: antenna was the yard of a ship's sail, a long spar reaching across the mast.
items.cn: antenna 指帆船上的横桁，是一根横过桅杆的长杆。

items.en: The Roman writer Pliny used antenna for the feelers of insects.
items.cn: 罗马作家普林尼用 antenna 指昆虫的触角。

items.en: Naturalists kept the insect sense alive in scientific descriptions.
items.cn: 博物学家在科学描述中保留了昆虫触角义。

items.en: English took antenna first as a term of natural history.
items.cn: 英语先把这个词用作博物学术语。

items.en: With radio, the old word was extended to the rods that send and catch waves.
items.cn: 随着无线电出现，这个旧词被扩展到发送与接收电波的金属杆。

items.en: Modern English uses the plural antennae for insects and antennas for aerials.
items.cn: 现代英语中昆虫多用复数 antennae，天线多用 antennas。

note.en: The first group gathers words that are close in spelling but unrelated in meaning; the second gathers words for feelers and wave receivers.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近但意义无关的词；第二组收表示触角与电波接收装置的词。

entries.definition: A song of praise or a national song.
A branched horn of a deer.
The insect plural, kept from Latin for feelers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，昆虫触角的复数，沿用拉丁形式。

entries.definition: A British word for the device that picks up radio or television signals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用法，义为「天线」，接收无线电或电视信号。

entries.definition: A general word for an animal's organ of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「触须」，泛指动物的触觉器官。

entries.definition: A tall pole that holds an aerial or a sail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桅杆、天线杆」，支撑天线或帆的高杆。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two plurals and the common aerial phrases; the abstract hooks picture a long feeler probing the air.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用两个复数形式与常见天线搭配；抽象记忆点想象一根细长触须在空中试探。

normal.en: Antennae is the insect plural, antennas the aerial plural.
normal.cn: antennae 是昆虫触角的复数，antennas 是天线的复数。

normal.en: A radio antenna catches waves; a satellite antenna faces the sky.
normal.cn: radio antenna 接收电波；satellite antenna 朝向天空。

normal.en: Latin antenna meant a sail yard before it meant a feeler.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 先指帆桁，后才指触角。

normal.en: The adjective is antennal, used in biology for feeler structures.
normal.cn: 形容词是 antennal，生物学中表示「触角的」。

normal.en: A good antenna for news is the figurative pattern worth remembering.
normal.cn: a good antenna for news 是值得记住的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture two thin whips tapping the air ahead of an ant.
abstract.cn: 想象两根细鞭在蚂蚁前方轻触空气。

abstract.en: Picture a long metal rod on a roof pointing at the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶上一根长金属杆指向地平线。

abstract.en: Picture a listener who senses a rumor before anyone says it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在别人开口前就嗅到传闻的听众。

examples.en: The moth's antennae detect the scent of a mate.
examples.cn: 飞蛾的触角能察觉配偶的气味。

examples.en: He climbed the roof to fix the television antenna.
examples.cn: 他爬上屋顶修理电视天线。

examples.en: She has an antenna for what the market will want next.
examples.cn: 她对市场下一步的需求有敏锐的嗅觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安泰娜」——头顶伸出两根细长探杆，在空气里四处试探，这就是触角。

root: 拉丁语 antenna（帆船横桁）→ 昆虫触角 → 无线电天线；核心义是「向外伸出、探测空中的细长装置」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the insect feeler, to the wireless aerial, to the figurative inner feeler for signals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从昆虫触角，走到无线电天线，再到比喻性的内在感知力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long feeler reaching out and probing the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根向外伸出并试探空气的长触须

branches.en: The insect's paired feelers for touch and scent.
branches.cn: 昆虫用于触觉与嗅觉的一对触角。

branches.en: The roof rod that sends and receives waves.
branches.cn: 屋顶上发送与接收电波的金属杆。

branches.en: A person's figurative feeler for trends and moods.
branches.cn: 一个人对趋势与情绪的比喻性触角。

branches.en: Both senses share the long outward-reaching shape.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享细长外伸的形状。

branches.en: Detection links the aerial and the inner sensor.
branches.cn: 「探测」把天线与内在感知连在一起。

intro.en: The word carries Latin antenna unchanged, and its family uses the adjective and diminutive endings -al and -ule.
intro.cn: 这个词原样保留拉丁语 antenna，其词族使用形容词与指小后缀 -al 与 -ule。

latinIntro.en: Latin antenna is the direct source, so the Latin entries record the sail-yard noun and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 是直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录「帆桁」名词与派生形容词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「触角的」
名词，义为「小触角」

definition_en: next to something, often sharing a border or wall
core_image: 两栋房子共用一道墙，门牌号挨着
scene: 地图上两个街区只隔一条窄巷，邮递员常把信送错门。The library is adjacent to the town hall.
sceneCN: 这里 adjacent 是「毗邻的、相邻的」（第 1 个义项：紧挨着并共享边界）；句意为图书馆毗邻市政厅。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ency 构成，义为「邻近；毗连」
加 -ly 构成，义为「相邻地」

senses.title: Next to and sharing a border
senses.definition: lying next to something, often sharing a wall or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，常共享墙或边界
senses.example: The library is adjacent to the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆毗邻市政厅。
senses.why: Latin adjacere meant 'to lie next to', so the adjective describes positions that touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adjacere 意为「躺在旁边」，因此这个形容词描述相互接触的位置。

senses.title: Nearby in a wider area
senses.definition: close to a place, not necessarily touching it
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某地，但不必相接
senses.example: The adjacent villages share one clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 邻近几个村庄共用一家诊所。
senses.why: Maps and planning use the word loosely for the next area over, even without a shared wall.
senses.whyCN: 地图与规划中这个词也宽松地指「旁边那一片」，即使没有共享墙面。

intro.en: Adjacent comes from Latin adjacere, 'to lie next to', from ad- 'to' and jacere, 'to lie'.
intro.cn: adjacent 来自拉丁语 adjacere（躺在旁边），由 ad-（向）与 jacere（躺）构成。

items.en: jacere meant 'to lie, to be thrown down'.
items.cn: jacere 意为「躺、被投下」。

items.en: adjacere meant 'to lie next to'.
items.cn: adjacere 意为「躺在旁边」。

items.en: adjacens meant 'lying near', the participle behind English.
items.cn: adjacens 意为「位于近旁的」，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: English adjacent first described lands lying side by side.
items.cn: 英语 adjacent 最初描述并排的土地。

items.en: modern usage adds adjacent rooms and adjacent areas.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了相邻房间与邻近区域。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun and adverb forms; the second gathers adjectives of near position.
note.cn: 第一组收名词与副词形式；第二组收表示邻近位置的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being next to.
The adverb meaning 'in a neighbouring position'.
An adjective for rooms that share a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毗连的」，常指共墙。

entries.definition: Located close to another place.
Close at hand.
Touching a border or edge.

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the 'lie next to' root and the shared wall; the abstract hooks picture two house numbers side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「躺在旁边」词根与共墙；抽象记忆点想象两个挨着的门牌号。

normal.en: Adjacent is 'lying next to': jacere means lie.
normal.cn: adjacent 是「躺在旁边」：jacere 意为躺。

normal.en: Adjacent to is the fixed preposition.
normal.cn: adjacent to 是固定介词搭配。

normal.en: Immediately adjacent means sharing a wall.
normal.cn: immediately adjacent 指共墙紧邻。

normal.en: The noun is adjacency, the adverb adjacently.
normal.cn: 名词是 adjacency，副词是 adjacently。

normal.en: Adjoining usually means touching; adjacent can be looser.
normal.cn: adjoining 通常指相接，adjacent 可以更宽松。

abstract.en: Picture two houses sharing one wall.
abstract.cn: 想象两栋房子共用一道墙。

abstract.en: Picture two numbers side by side on a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门上挨着的两个门牌号。

abstract.en: Picture a map with two blocks split by an alley.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上被窄巷分开的两个街区。

examples.en: The library is adjacent to the town hall.
examples.cn: 图书馆毗邻市政厅。

examples.en: The adjacent villages share one clinic.
examples.cn: 邻近几个村庄共用一家诊所。

examples.en: Parking is available in the adjacent building.
examples.cn: 相邻建筑内有停车位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿杰森特」——像两户人家共用一堵墙那样挨着，就是相邻。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ jacere（躺）→ adjacere；核心义是「躺在旁边、彼此相接」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from sharing a border, to being merely nearby.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从共享边界，走到仅仅在附近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two houses sharing one wall
core.cn: 核心意象：两栋房子共用一道墙

branches.en: Next to something and sharing a border.
branches.cn: 紧挨着并共享边界。

branches.en: Close to a place in a wider sense.
branches.cn: 更宽泛意义上的靠近。

branches.en: The strict and loose senses differ by contact.
branches.cn: 严格义与宽松义差别在是否接触。

branches.en: Maps often use the looser sense.
branches.cn: 地图常用较宽松的义项。

branches.en: Both rest on the image of lying beside.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立足在「躺在旁边」的意象。

intro.en: The adjective joins the prefix ad- (to) with the lie root jac- and the participle ending -ent.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把前缀 ad-（向）与「躺」词根 jac- 及分词后缀 -ent 结合。

latinIntro.en: Latin adjacens is the direct ancestor, recorded here with jacere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adjacens 是直接祖先，这里连同 jacere 一并记录。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「邻近」
副词，义为「相邻地」
